qualifiers.definition: Many nerves, diffusely and symmetrically
qualifiers.established: Symmetric length-dependent deficits on examination
qualifiers.example: symmetric distal polyneuropathy → diabetes
qualifiers.shift: Symmetric, length-dependent involvement favors systemic metabolic or toxic causes.

qualifiers.name: Length-dependent
qualifiers.definition: Longest nerves affected first
qualifiers.established: Establish the level in legs and arms and compare
qualifiers.example: numbness reaching the knees before the fingers → axonal polyneuropathy
qualifiers.shift: The stocking-glove progression with feet involved well before hands. Strongly favors metabolic or toxic axonal neuropathy over demyelinating or root disease.

qualifiers.name: Stocking-glove
qualifiers.definition: Distal symmetric sensory loss
qualifiers.established: Mapping the sensory boundary in all four limbs
qualifiers.example: stocking-glove sensory loss → diabetic polyneuropathy
qualifiers.shift: Same implication as length-dependent, expressed as a distribution.

qualifiers.name: Radicular
qualifiers.definition: Spinal nerve root origin
qualifiers.established: Match pain dermatome, weak myotome, and absent reflex
qualifiers.example: dermatomal leg pain with a lost ankle reflex → S1 radiculopathy
qualifiers.shift: Pain in a dermatome with weakness in a myotome and a lost reflex localizes to a single root and directs targeted imaging.

qualifiers.name: Myelopathic
qualifiers.definition: Spinal cord dysfunction
qualifiers.established: Tone, reflexes, sensory level, and sphincter assessment
qualifiers.associated: Cervical stenosis, MS, B12 deficiency, cord compression
qualifiers.example: spastic gait with a sensory level → cord compression
qualifiers.shift: A sensory level, bladder involvement, or a spastic gait with hyperreflexia below a level is a cord emergency until imaged.
qualifiers.misuse: Imaging delayed for a full workup; cord compression is time-critical

qualifiers.name: Cerebellar
qualifiers.definition: Cerebellar localization
qualifiers.established: Finger-to-nose, dysdiadochokinesia, gait
qualifiers.example: dysmetria with intention tremor → cerebellar infarct
qualifiers.shift: Dysmetria, intention tremor, nystagmus. Acute cerebellar stroke can cause fatal swelling, so this localization is time-critical.

qualifiers.name: Parkinsonian
qualifiers.definition: Bradykinesia with rigidity or rest tremor
qualifiers.established: Test for decrement in repetitive movements, plus tone and tremor
qualifiers.example: bradykinesia with rest tremor → Parkinson disease
qualifiers.shift: Bradykinesia is required. Symmetric onset, early falls, or poor levodopa response argue against idiopathic Parkinson disease and toward an atypical syndrome or drug effect.
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed from tremor alone; bradykinesia is required

qualifiers.name: Encephalopathic
qualifiers.definition: Global cerebral dysfunction
qualifiers.established: Attention testing plus a nonfocal neurologic examination
qualifiers.associated: Sepsis, hepatic and uremic failure, drugs
qualifiers.example: global inattention without focal signs → metabolic encephalopathy
qualifiers.shift: Global rather than focal. Directs toward systemic, metabolic, and toxic causes rather than a structural lesion, though structural causes still require exclusion.

qualifiers.name: Toxic-metabolic
qualifiers.definition: Due to toxins or systemic metabolic derangement
qualifiers.established: Nonfocal exam, asterixis, and targeted metabolic labs
qualifiers.example: asterixis with confusion → hepatic encephalopathy
qualifiers.shift: Predicts a non-focal exam with preserved pupillary reflexes and asterixis, and predicts reversibility if the cause is corrected.
qualifiers.misuse: Structural causes assumed excluded without imaging in a patient with focal signs

qualifiers.name: Ascending
qualifiers.definition: Progressing upward from the lower body
qualifiers.established: Serial examination documenting upward progression
qualifiers.example: ascending areflexic weakness → Guillain-Barré syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Ascending symmetric weakness with areflexia is GBS until proven otherwise, and mandates serial vital capacity measurement rather than pulse oximetry.
qualifiers.misuse: Monitored with pulse oximetry; vital capacity is the measure that matters

qualifiers.name: Descending
qualifiers.definition: Progressing downward from cranial muscles
qualifiers.established: Serial examination documenting downward progression
qualifiers.example: descending paralysis with early bulbar signs → botulism
qualifiers.shift: Descending paralysis with early bulbar and pupillary involvement points to botulism, a very different diagnosis with a very different treatment.

qualifiers.name: Monocular
qualifiers.definition: One eye
qualifiers.established: Test each eye separately with the other covered
qualifiers.associated: Retinal artery occlusion, optic neuritis, amaurosis fugax
qualifiers.example: monocular visual loss → central retinal artery occlusion
qualifiers.shift: Localizes anterior to the optic chiasm, meaning eye or optic nerve.
qualifiers.misuse: Patients report binocular field loss as one-eye loss unless each eye is tested

qualifiers.name: Binocular
qualifiers.definition: Both eyes or the visual pathways
qualifiers.established: Ask whether covering either eye abolishes it
qualifiers.example: binocular diplopia → ocular motor cranial neuropathy
qualifiers.shift: Localizes at or behind the chiasm. Binocular diplopia that resolves on covering either eye is an ocular motor problem, not a retinal one.

qualifiers.name: Transient
qualifiers.definition: Complete resolution after a short time
qualifiers.established: Complete return to baseline documented by history
qualifiers.example: transient monocular visual loss → amaurosis fugax
qualifiers.shift: Full resolution suggests a vascular or electrical event rather than structural injury, and makes secondary prevention the priority.

qualifiers.name: Positive symptom
qualifiers.definition: An added abnormal phenomenon
qualifiers.established: Ask whether something was added or lost
qualifiers.example: marching visual scintillations → migraine aura
qualifiers.shift: Positive phenomena imply cortical excitation or spreading depression, favoring seizure and migraine over ischemia.

qualifiers.name: Negative symptom
qualifiers.definition: Loss of normal function
qualifiers.established: Ask whether function was lost rather than added
qualifiers.example: sudden painless field loss → retinal or cerebral ischemia
qualifiers.shift: Loss of function implies ischemia or structural interruption. The positive-versus-negative distinction is the fastest way to separate aura from TIA at the bedside.

qualifiers.name: Fatigable
qualifiers.definition: Worsening with sustained or repeated effort, improving with rest
qualifiers.established: Sustained upgaze for sixty seconds, or repetitive proximal movement
qualifiers.example: fatigable ptosis → myasthenia gravis
qualifiers.shift: Nearly specific for the neuromuscular junction. Test it: sustained upgaze for a minute, or repeated proximal movements. Lambert-Eaton shows the opposite, transient facilitation with brief exercise.
qualifiers.misuse: Not tested; a single-timepoint exam looks normal

qualifiers.name: Rest tremor
qualifiers.definition: Present at rest, damped by voluntary movement
qualifiers.established: Observe hands at rest fully supported, with mental distraction
qualifiers.example: pill-rolling rest tremor → Parkinson disease
qualifiers.shift: Improvement with action is the discriminator. Combined with bradykinesia and rigidity it defines parkinsonism.
qualifiers.misuse: Not observed at true rest, so it disappears

qualifiers.name: Postural tremor
qualifiers.definition: Appears when holding a position against gravity
qualifiers.established: Arms outstretched against gravity
qualifiers.example: postural hand tremor → essential tremor
qualifiers.shift: Bilateral postural tremor of the hands improving with alcohol and with a family history suggests essential tremor rather than Parkinson disease.

qualifiers.name: Intention tremor
qualifiers.definition: Worsens as the limb approaches a target
qualifiers.established: Finger-to-nose watching for amplification near the target
qualifiers.example: terminal intention tremor → cerebellar disease
qualifiers.shift: Terminal amplification on finger-to-nose localizes to the cerebellum or its outflow, a different lesion entirely from the other two tremors.

qualifiers.name: Cortical
qualifiers.definition: Signs referable to cerebral cortex
qualifiers.established: Test language, neglect, praxis, and cortical sensation
qualifiers.example: aphasia with neglect → large-vessel cortical infarct
qualifiers.shift: Aphasia, neglect, apraxia, agnosia, and cortical sensory loss localize above the subcortical structures and, in stroke, imply large-vessel territory.

qualifiers.name: Subcortical
qualifiers.definition: Signs referable to deep structures and white matter
qualifiers.established: Cognitive testing showing executive and speed deficits without aphasia
qualifiers.example: slowed processing with gait apraxia → small-vessel disease
qualifiers.shift: Slowed processing, executive dysfunction, and gait disturbance without aphasia or neglect. In stroke, favors small-vessel disease.

qualifiers.name: Fluent aphasia
qualifiers.definition: Preserved output with impaired comprehension
qualifiers.established: Assess fluency, comprehension, and repetition separately
qualifiers.example: fluent speech with impaired comprehension → Wernicke aphasia
qualifiers.shift: Localizes posteriorly. Often mistaken for confusion or psychosis, which is a well-documented and consequential error.
qualifiers.misuse: Mistaken for delirium or psychosis, which delays stroke recognition

qualifiers.name: Nonfluent aphasia
qualifiers.definition: Effortful sparse output with relatively preserved comprehension
qualifiers.established: Assess fluency, comprehension, and repetition separately
qualifiers.example: effortful sparse speech → Broca aphasia
qualifiers.shift: Localizes anteriorly and frequently accompanies right hemiparesis given the proximity of motor cortex.

qualifiers.name: Postictal
qualifiers.definition: The recovery state following a seizure
qualifiers.established: Witnessed event plus gradual clearing over minutes to hours
qualifiers.example: transient hemiparesis after a witnessed seizure → Todd paralysis
qualifiers.shift: Gradual clearing over minutes to hours, and a focal postictal deficit (Todd paralysis) can mimic stroke. Recognizing it prevents unnecessary thrombolysis but must not be assumed without a witnessed event.
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed without a witnessed seizure, which risks withholding stroke therapy

qualifiers.name: Focal aware and focal impaired awareness
qualifiers.definition: Seizure without or with loss of awareness
qualifiers.established: Ask a witness whether the patient was aware and responsive throughout
qualifiers.example: focal impaired-awareness seizure → temporal lobe epilepsy
qualifiers.shift: Current ILAE terminology, replacing simple and complex partial. Awareness during the event, not motor features, is the classifying axis.
qualifiers.misuse: Classified by motor features rather than by awareness

qualifiers.name: Meningismus
qualifiers.definition: Neck stiffness with photophobia and headache
qualifiers.established: Passive neck flexion with the patient supine
qualifiers.example: neck stiffness with fever → bacterial meningitis
qualifiers.shift: Raises meningitis and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Note its sensitivity is poor, particularly in the elderly and immunosuppressed, so absence does not exclude either.
qualifiers.misuse: Poor sensitivity in the elderly and immunosuppressed; absence does not exclude meningitis

qualifiers.name: Steppage gait
qualifiers.definition: High-stepping to clear a foot that will not dorsiflex
qualifiers.established: Observe walking and heel walking
qualifiers.example: high-stepping gait → foot drop from peroneal palsy
qualifiers.shift: Indicates foot drop and directs attention to the peroneal nerve, L5 root, or a length-dependent neuropathy.

qualifiers.name: Waddling gait
qualifiers.definition: Pelvic drop with each step from hip girdle weakness
qualifiers.established: Observe gait and test hip girdle power
qualifiers.example: waddling gait → proximal myopathy
qualifiers.shift: A proximal weakness sign, consistent with myopathy rather than neuropathy.

qualifiers.name: Direction-fixed nystagmus
qualifiers.definition: Fast phase beats the same way regardless of gaze
qualifiers.established: Observe nystagmus in several gaze positions
qualifiers.example: direction-fixed horizontal nystagmus → vestibular neuritis
qualifiers.shift: Favors a peripheral cause such as vestibular neuritis. Combined with an abnormal head impulse test and no skew, it argues against stroke.

qualifiers.name: Direction-changing nystagmus
qualifiers.definition: Fast phase reverses with gaze direction
qualifiers.established: Observe in right and left gaze for reversal
qualifiers.example: direction-changing nystagmus → posterior circulation stroke
qualifiers.shift: A central sign. With vertical or torsional nystagmus, skew deviation, or a normal head impulse test, treat as posterior circulation stroke until imaged.
qualifiers.misuse: Only primary gaze is examined, so direction change is missed

qualifiers.name: Skew deviation
qualifiers.definition: Vertical misalignment of the eyes
qualifiers.established: Alternate cover test looking for vertical correction
qualifiers.example: skew deviation → brainstem lesion
qualifiers.shift: One of the three HINTS components and a central sign. Its presence in acute vestibular syndrome substantially raises stroke probability.

qualifiers.name: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia
qualifiers.definition: Impaired adduction with nystagmus of the abducting eye
qualifiers.established: Horizontal saccades watching for adduction lag with abducting nystagmus
qualifiers.example: bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia → multiple sclerosis
qualifiers.shift: Localizes precisely to the medial longitudinal fasciculus. Bilateral INO in a young patient is close to diagnostic of MS.

qualifiers.name: Relative afferent pupillary defect
qualifiers.definition: Paradoxical dilation on swinging flashlight test
qualifiers.established: Swinging flashlight test in a dimly lit room
qualifiers.associated: Optic neuritis, ischemic optic neuropathy, dense retinal disease
qualifiers.example: right afferent pupillary defect → optic neuritis
qualifiers.shift: Objective evidence of asymmetric optic nerve dysfunction. Cannot be feigned, and localizes anterior to the chiasm.
qualifiers.misuse: Attempted in a bright room, where the response is not visible

qualifiers.name: False localizing sign
qualifiers.definition: A finding that suggests a lesion elsewhere than its true site
qualifiers.established: Recognizing a finding inconsistent with the rest of the localization
qualifiers.associated: Sixth nerve palsy with raised intracranial pressure
qualifiers.example: abducens palsy with papilledema → raised intracranial pressure
qualifiers.shift: Prevents a serious error. An abducens palsy from raised pressure does not indicate a pontine lesion, and treating it as localizing sends the workup in the wrong direction.
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as localizing, sending imaging to the wrong territory

qualifiers.name: Give-way weakness
qualifiers.definition: Effort that starts strong then abruptly collapses
qualifiers.established: Hoover sign and testing for inconsistency across tasks
qualifiers.example: give-way weakness with a positive Hoover sign → functional weakness
qualifiers.shift: Inconsistent effort suggests functional or pain-limited weakness rather than a fixed lesion, but pain and poor comprehension must be excluded before concluding.
qualifiers.misuse: Interpreted as feigning; functional disorders are involuntary

qualifiers.name: Pyramidal distribution weakness
qualifiers.definition: Upper limb extensors and lower limb flexors preferentially weak
qualifiers.established: Compare upper limb extensors with flexors and the reverse in the legs
qualifiers.example: pyramidal pattern weakness → corticospinal tract lesion
qualifiers.shift: Distinguishes an upper motor neuron pattern from a myopathic or neuropathic one on exam alone.

qualifiers.name: Spasticity
qualifiers.definition: Velocity-dependent resistance with a catch and release
qualifiers.established: Move the limb fast, then slow, and compare
qualifiers.example: velocity-dependent catch → upper motor neuron lesion
qualifiers.shift: Velocity dependence separates it from rigidity and localizes to the corticospinal tract.

qualifiers.name: Rigidity
qualifiers.definition: Resistance uniform through the range, independent of velocity
qualifiers.established: Slow passive movement, augmented by contralateral voluntary movement
qualifiers.example: cogwheel rigidity → parkinsonism
qualifiers.shift: Lead-pipe or cogwheel quality points to basal ganglia disease rather than corticospinal disease.
qualifiers.misuse: Not augmented, so mild rigidity is missed

qualifiers.name: Paratonia
qualifiers.definition: Variable resistance that increases with the examiner's effort
qualifiers.established: Passive movement at varying speeds with the patient relaxed
qualifiers.example: paratonia → diffuse frontal dysfunction
qualifiers.shift: Often mistaken for rigidity or voluntary resistance. Suggests diffuse frontal or global cerebral dysfunction.
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded as rigidity or as poor cooperation

qualifiers.name: Asterixis
qualifiers.definition: Brief lapses of postural tone, a negative myoclonus
qualifiers.established: Wrists extended, arms outstretched, held for thirty seconds
qualifiers.example: asterixis → hepatic or uremic encephalopathy
qualifiers.shift: A loss of tone rather than an added movement, which is why it appears in metabolic encephalopathies and not in most structural lesions.
qualifiers.misuse: Tested too briefly; it may take twenty to thirty seconds to appear

qualifiers.name: Fasciculations
qualifiers.definition: Spontaneous visible twitches of motor units
qualifiers.established: Observe relaxed muscle, including the tongue at rest in the mouth
qualifiers.example: tongue fasciculations with limb atrophy → amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
qualifiers.shift: Fasciculations with weakness and atrophy suggest motor neuron disease; fasciculations alone in a well patient are usually benign. Tongue involvement is particularly concerning.
qualifiers.misuse: Tongue examined protruded, which produces normal tremor mistaken for fasciculation

qualifiers.name: Albuminocytologic dissociation
qualifiers.definition: Elevated CSF protein with a normal cell count
qualifiers.established: Lumbar puncture with protein and cell count
qualifiers.example: raised CSF protein with normal cell count → Guillain-Barré syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Close to characteristic for acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculopathy, though frequently absent in the first week, so a normal early study does not exclude GBS.
qualifiers.misuse: Often absent in the first week; a normal early study does not exclude GBS

qualifiers.name: Lymphocytic pleocytosis
qualifiers.definition: Raised CSF white cells, lymphocyte predominant
qualifiers.established: CSF cell count with differential
qualifiers.associated: Viral meningitis, TB, neurosyphilis, autoimmune encephalitis
qualifiers.example: lymphocytic pleocytosis → viral or tuberculous meningitis
qualifiers.shift: Shifts away from bacterial meningitis toward viral, mycobacterial, fungal, and autoimmune causes, and changes empiric therapy and additional testing.

qualifiers.name: Neutrophilic pleocytosis
qualifiers.definition: Raised CSF white cells, neutrophil predominant
qualifiers.established: CSF cell count, glucose, and protein
qualifiers.example: neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose → bacterial meningitis
qualifiers.shift: With low glucose and high protein this is bacterial meningitis until cultures return. Note that very early viral meningitis can be neutrophilic.
qualifiers.misuse: Very early viral meningitis can be neutrophilic

qualifiers.name: Xanthochromia
qualifiers.definition: Yellow discoloration of centrifuged CSF supernatant
qualifiers.established: Spectrophotometry or visual inspection of centrifuged supernatant
qualifiers.example: xanthochromic CSF → subarachnoid hemorrhage
qualifiers.shift: Distinguishes true subarachnoid blood from a traumatic tap, because it requires hours for hemoglobin breakdown. Sensitivity rises after about twelve hours.
qualifiers.misuse: Sampled too early; sensitivity rises after about twelve hours

qualifiers.name: Oligoclonal bands
qualifiers.definition: CSF-restricted immunoglobulin bands not present in serum
qualifiers.established: Paired CSF and serum electrophoresis
qualifiers.example: CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands → multiple sclerosis
qualifiers.shift: Evidence of intrathecal antibody synthesis. Supports MS and now substitutes for dissemination in time in the diagnostic criteria.
qualifiers.misuse: Serum not sent in parallel, so CSF restriction cannot be established

qualifiers.name: Areflexic
qualifiers.definition: Deep tendon reflexes absent rather than merely reduced
qualifiers.established: Test with reinforcement before recording a reflex as absent
qualifiers.associated: Guillain-Barré, severe peripheral neuropathy, spinal shock
qualifiers.example: ascending weakness that is areflexic → Guillain-Barré syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Localizes to the reflex arc, so it separates a peripheral or root lesion from an upper motor neuron one. Areflexia with ascending weakness is the combination that mandates vital capacity monitoring
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded without reinforcement, so a present reflex is called absent

qualifiers.name: Photophobic
qualifiers.definition: Light provokes or worsens pain
qualifiers.established: Ask about light sensitivity, and observe the response to an ophthalmoscope light
qualifiers.associated: Meningitis, subarachnoid hemorrhage, migraine, anterior uveitis, corneal disease
qualifiers.example: photophobia with ciliary flush and a small pupil → acute anterior uveitis
qualifiers.shift: Splits into intracranial and ocular causes. With meningismus it points to the meninges; with a red eye and ciliary flush it points to the anterior chamber
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed meningeal, so a red painful eye is not examined

qualifiers.name: Hyperreflexia
qualifiers.definition: Exaggerated deep tendon reflexes, often with a spread of the reflexogenic zone or clonus
qualifiers.established: Tendon hammer with the limb relaxed; compare sides and levels, and test for clonus at the ankle
qualifiers.associated: Upper motor neuron lesions, serotonin syndrome, hyperthyroidism, preeclampsia, hepatic encephalopathy
qualifiers.example: hyperreflexia with clonus and agitation → serotonin syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Localizes to the upper motor neuron when focal, but when generalized and acute it points instead at a metabolic or toxidromic cause, which is where it is most often missed
qualifiers.misuse: Compared against a textbook rather than the patient's other side; a symmetric brisk reflex can be normal

qualifiers.name: Ophthalmoplegia
qualifiers.definition: Impaired movement of one or both eyes
qualifiers.established: Test ductions and versions in all directions; note whether the pattern fits a single nerve, a muscle, or a supranuclear lesion
qualifiers.associated: Third, fourth and sixth nerve palsies, myasthenia gravis, thyroid eye disease, Wernicke encephalopathy, cavernous sinus disease
qualifiers.example: ophthalmoplegia with ataxia and confusion → Wernicke encephalopathy
qualifiers.shift: The pattern is what localizes. A pupil-involving third nerve palsy is a compressive aneurysm until excluded, while fatigable and variable weakness crossing nerve territories points at the neuromuscular junction
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to a single nerve without testing all directions, missing the multiple-territory pattern that indicates cavernous sinus or orbital disease

qualifiers.name: Pinpoint pupils
qualifiers.definition: Bilateral pupillary constriction to 2 mm or less
qualifiers.established: Inspect in dim light; use a magnifier if needed
qualifiers.associated: Opioid toxicity, pontine hemorrhage, cholinergic toxicity, clonidine overdose
qualifiers.example: pinpoint pupils with respiratory depression → opioid toxicity
qualifiers.shift: With depressed consciousness and a low respiratory rate this completes the opioid toxidrome and justifies naloxone. In a comatose patient without opioid exposure, pontine hemorrhage is the alternative that must not be missed
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed in bright light, where normal constriction is mistaken for the finding

qualifiers.name: Mydriasis
qualifiers.definition: Bilateral pupillary dilatation
qualifiers.established: Inspect in dim light, checking the reaction to light and near
qualifiers.associated: Anticholinergic toxicity, sympathomimetic toxicity, serotonin syndrome, brain death, topical agents
qualifiers.example: mydriasis with dry flushed skin and delirium → anticholinergic toxicity
qualifiers.shift: Splits by sweating: anticholinergic toxicity gives dry skin and urinary retention, sympathomimetic toxicity gives diaphoresis. This distinction changes the antidote
qualifiers.misuse: Unilateral dilatation grouped with bilateral; a single blown pupil is an anatomic emergency, not a toxidrome

qualifiers.name: Magnetic gait
qualifiers.definition: A slow, shuffling, wide-based gait in which the feet seem stuck to the floor, with difficulty initiating steps
qualifiers.established: Observe walking, turning and initiation over several metres
qualifiers.example: magnetic gait with incontinence and cognitive slowing → normal pressure hydrocephalus
qualifiers.shift: Completes a triad in which the gait typically comes first and responds best to shunting, so recognizing it early is what determines whether the syndrome is reversible
qualifiers.misuse: Called parkinsonian; the arm swing is usually preserved and there is no rest tremor, which is the separating detail

qualifiers.name: Posterior column signs
qualifiers.definition: Loss of vibration and proprioception with a positive Romberg, sparing pain and temperature
qualifiers.established: 128 Hz tuning fork at the malleolus, joint position sense at the great toe, Romberg test
qualifiers.associated: B12 deficiency, tabes dorsalis, copper deficiency, nitrous oxide misuse
qualifiers.example: posterior column signs → subacute combined degeneration
qualifiers.shift: A dissociated sensory loss localizes to a tract rather than a nerve, which points at the cord and, with pyramidal signs, at subacute combined degeneration
qualifiers.misuse: Romberg read as a cerebellar test; it is positive in proprioceptive loss, and a patient unsteady with eyes open has a different problem

qualifiers.name: Kayser-Fleischer rings
qualifiers.definition: Golden-brown copper deposition at the corneal limbus, in Descemet membrane
qualifiers.established: Slit lamp examination; frequently invisible to the naked eye
qualifiers.example: Kayser-Fleischer rings with a movement disorder → Wilson disease
qualifiers.shift: In a young patient with neuropsychiatric or hepatic disease this is close to diagnostic, and it is present in nearly all cases with neurologic involvement
qualifiers.misuse: Excluded on penlight examination; the finding requires a slit lamp and its absence does not exclude hepatic Wilson disease

qualifiers.name: Argyll Robertson pupils
qualifiers.definition: Small irregular pupils that accommodate but do not react to light
qualifiers.established: Test light reaction and then the near response separately
qualifiers.example: Argyll Robertson pupils → neurosyphilis
qualifiers.shift: Light-near dissociation localizes to the pretectal region and, in the right context, is a classic sign of tertiary syphilis
qualifiers.misuse: Not elicited because the near response is never tested separately from light

qualifiers.name: Waxy flexibility
qualifiers.definition: Limbs retain a position into which they are passively placed, against gravity
qualifiers.established: Passively move a limb and release it, observing whether the posture is held
qualifiers.example: waxy flexibility with mutism → catatonia
qualifiers.shift: Identifies catatonia, which is a treatable syndrome that arises as often from medical and mood disorders as from schizophrenia and responds to benzodiazepines
qualifiers.misuse: Interpreted as volitional or as a functional disorder, delaying a lorazepam challenge

qualifiers.name: Ataxia
qualifiers.definition: Incoordination of movement not explained by weakness
qualifiers.established: Finger-nose and heel-shin testing, gait and tandem gait, and Romberg to separate cerebellar from sensory causes
qualifiers.associated: Cerebellar stroke, alcohol and thiamine deficiency, posterior fossa tumour, sensory neuropathy, drug toxicity
qualifiers.example: ataxia with ophthalmoplegia and confusion → Wernicke encephalopathy
qualifiers.shift: Splits into cerebellar, sensory and vestibular. A positive Romberg indicates a sensory cause, while cerebellar ataxia is unsteady with eyes open and closed alike
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to intoxication in an alcohol-dependent patient, which is how Wernicke encephalopathy is missed

qualifiers.name: Bradykinesia
qualifiers.definition: Slowness of movement with progressive decrement in amplitude on repetition
qualifiers.established: Repetitive finger tapping or hand opening and closing, watching for decrement rather than simple slowness
qualifiers.associated: Parkinson disease, drug-induced parkinsonism, vascular parkinsonism, progressive supranuclear palsy
qualifiers.example: bradykinesia with rest tremor and rigidity → Parkinson disease
qualifiers.shift: The obligatory feature for a parkinsonian syndrome; the decrement is what separates it from the general slowness of depression or hypothyroidism
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded as slowness without testing repetition, which is where the decrement appears

qualifiers.name: Altered mental state
qualifiers.definition: A change in arousal, attention, or cognition from the patient's baseline
qualifiers.established: Establish the baseline from someone who knows the patient, then test attention formally
qualifiers.associated: Delirium, meningitis, intoxication, hypoglycaemia, non-convulsive status, sepsis
qualifiers.example: altered mental state with fever and neck stiffness → bacterial meningitis
qualifiers.shift: Almost always a systemic problem rather than a primary neurologic one, particularly in the elderly, where it may be the only presenting feature of infection or infarction
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded without a baseline, which makes it uninterpretable and is how dementia is mistaken for delirium

qualifiers.name: Proptosis
qualifiers.definition: Forward protrusion of the globe
qualifiers.established: Look from above and behind the seated patient; measure with an exophthalmometer
qualifiers.associated: Thyroid eye disease, orbital cellulitis, orbital tumour, carotid-cavernous fistula
qualifiers.example: proptosis with lid retraction → thyroid eye disease
qualifiers.shift: Bilateral and painless suggests thyroid eye disease; unilateral, painful and acute suggests orbital cellulitis or a vascular lesion and is an emergency
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed face-on, where mild asymmetry is invisible

qualifiers.name: Uveitis
qualifiers.definition: Inflammation of the uveal tract, presenting with a painful red eye, photophobia, and reduced vision
qualifiers.established: Slit lamp examination for cells and flare; visual acuity in both eyes
qualifiers.associated: Ankylosing spondylitis and other HLA-B27 disease, sarcoidosis, Behcet disease, inflammatory bowel disease, infection
qualifiers.example: anterior uveitis with back pain → ankylosing spondylitis
qualifiers.shift: A red eye that is painful with photophobia and reduced vision is not conjunctivitis. Recurrent uveitis is frequently the first evidence of a systemic inflammatory disease
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as conjunctivitis with topical antibiotics, delaying the steroid that prevents synechiae

qualifiers.name: Clonus
qualifiers.definition: Rhythmic involuntary contractions elicited by sudden sustained stretch
qualifiers.established: Sharp dorsiflexion of the ankle with the knee slightly flexed; count the beats and note whether they sustain
qualifiers.associated: Upper motor neuron lesions, serotonin syndrome, preeclampsia, hepatic encephalopathy
qualifiers.example: sustained clonus with agitation and diaphoresis → serotonin syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Sustained clonus indicates a genuine upper motor neuron process, while a few unsustained beats can be normal in an anxious patient. Clonus is the pivotal sign in the Hunter criteria for serotonin syndrome: spontaneous clonus alone is sufficient, while inducible clonus counts only alongside agitation or diaphoresis
qualifiers.misuse: Two or three beats reported as clonus; the finding that matters is sustained or clearly asymmetric

qualifiers.name: Delirium
qualifiers.definition: An acute, fluctuating disturbance of attention and awareness
qualifiers.established: Test attention formally, months of the year backwards or digit span; establish the baseline from a collateral source
qualifiers.associated: Infection, drugs, metabolic derangement, hypoxia, pain, urinary retention, alcohol withdrawal
qualifiers.example: fluctuating inattention over hours → delirium
qualifiers.shift: Acuity and fluctuation separate it from dementia, which is chronic and stable day to day. Hypoactive delirium is commoner than the agitated form and is routinely missed because a quiet patient does not attract attention
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed as dementia in an older adult without a collateral history, which is how a treatable cause is left untreated

qualifiers.name: Dementia
qualifiers.definition: A chronic, progressive decline in cognition sufficient to impair function
qualifiers.established: Collateral history over months to years, plus formal cognitive testing when the patient is at their baseline
qualifiers.associated: Alzheimer disease, vascular dementia, Lewy body dementia, frontotemporal dementia, normal pressure hydrocephalus
qualifiers.example: progressive cognitive decline with visual hallucinations and parkinsonism → Lewy body dementia
qualifiers.shift: Chronic and progressive, which is what separates it from delirium. The pattern of first deficit matters: memory in Alzheimer, behaviour in frontotemporal, attention and hallucinations in Lewy body
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed during an acute illness, when delirium makes cognitive testing uninterpretable

qualifiers.name: Visual hallucinations
qualifiers.definition: Perception of visual images without an external stimulus
qualifiers.established: Ask directly and without judgement; ask whether the patient knows they are not real
qualifiers.associated: Lewy body dementia, delirium, alcohol withdrawal, Charles Bonnet syndrome, occipital lesions
qualifiers.example: well-formed visual hallucinations with parkinsonism → Lewy body dementia
qualifiers.shift: Visual hallucinations point away from primary psychiatric illness, where auditory hallucinations dominate, and toward a neurologic or toxic cause. Well-formed recurrent ones with fluctuating cognition suggest Lewy body dementia
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to psychosis and treated with an antipsychotic, which in Lewy body dementia can cause severe neuroleptic sensitivity

qualifiers.name: Delusions
qualifiers.definition: Fixed false beliefs held against evidence and outside cultural norm
qualifiers.established: Explore the belief gently, testing whether it is fixed and whether it is culturally sanctioned
qualifiers.associated: Schizophrenia, bipolar mania, psychotic depression, delirium, dementia, stimulant toxicity
qualifiers.example: persecutory delusions with disorganized thought and negative symptoms → schizophrenia
qualifiers.shift: Content is less useful than fixity. Delusions with a clear sensorium point at a primary psychotic illness, while delusions with fluctuating attention point at delirium and demand a medical workup
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed as psychiatric before a medical cause is excluded, which is how encephalitis and thyroid disease are missed

qualifiers.name: Disorganized thought
qualifiers.definition: Speech that fails to follow logical connections: tangentiality, derailment, or word salad
qualifiers.established: Listen to spontaneous speech and note whether answers connect to questions
qualifiers.example: disorganized thought with delusions and negative symptoms → schizophrenia
qualifiers.shift: A form abnormality rather than a content one, which makes it harder to feign and more specific for genuine psychosis. Its presence alongside preserved attention favours a primary psychotic illness over delirium
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with the pressured tangential speech of mania, where the thread is fast but traceable

qualifiers.name: Negative symptoms
qualifiers.definition: Loss of normal function: flat affect, avolition, alogia, asociality, anhedonia
qualifiers.established: Observe affect and volition over time; ask a collateral source about withdrawal from usual activity
qualifiers.associated: Schizophrenia, depression, Parkinson disease, frontal lobe injury, medication effect
qualifiers.example: negative symptoms with delusions and disorganized thought → schizophrenia
qualifiers.shift: They predict long-term function better than positive symptoms and respond far less well to antipsychotics. Distinguishing them from depression and from medication-induced parkinsonism changes treatment entirely
qualifiers.misuse: Mistaken for depression or for laziness, delaying recognition of the more disabling half of the illness

qualifiers.name: Anhedonia
qualifiers.definition: Loss of the capacity to experience pleasure from previously enjoyed activity
qualifiers.established: Ask what the patient used to enjoy and whether they still do
qualifiers.associated: Major depressive episode, schizophrenia, Parkinson disease, substance withdrawal
qualifiers.example: anhedonia with low mood for two weeks → major depressive episode
qualifiers.shift: One of the two core criteria for a depressive episode, alongside low mood, and its presence carries more diagnostic weight than the somatic symptoms, which overlap heavily with physical illness
qualifiers.misuse: Merged with fatigue; a patient can want to and be too tired, which is different from not wanting to

qualifiers.name: Mutism
qualifiers.definition: Absence of speech in a patient who is awake
qualifiers.established: Distinguish from aphasia by testing comprehension and writing, and from unresponsiveness by assessing arousal
qualifiers.associated: Catatonia, severe depression, akinetic mutism, aphasia, selective mutism
qualifiers.example: mutism with waxy flexibility and negativism → catatonia
qualifiers.shift: With other catatonic features it identifies a treatable syndrome that responds to benzodiazepines. Preserved comprehension separates it from aphasia, which localises to the dominant hemisphere
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed to be uncooperativeness, delaying a lorazepam challenge that is both diagnostic and therapeutic

qualifiers.name: Negativism
qualifiers.definition: Motiveless resistance to instruction or to attempts to be moved, sometimes doing the opposite
qualifiers.established: Ask the patient to perform a simple action and observe resistance; attempt gentle passive movement
qualifiers.example: negativism with mutism → catatonia
qualifiers.shift: Part of the catatonic syndrome, which arises from mood disorders and general medical illness at least as often as from schizophrenia and is reversible when recognised
qualifiers.misuse: Read as refusal or as behavioural, which is exactly the interpretation that delays treatment

qualifiers.name: Parkinsonism
qualifiers.definition: The syndrome of bradykinesia in combination with rest tremor, rigidity, or both. Postural instability is not part of the defining triad
qualifiers.established: Test for decrement on repetitive movement, assess tone, observe gait and postural reflexes
qualifiers.associated: Parkinson disease, drug-induced parkinsonism, Lewy body dementia, progressive supranuclear palsy, multiple system atrophy, vascular parkinsonism
qualifiers.example: parkinsonism with early falls and restricted upgaze → progressive supranuclear palsy
qualifiers.shift: A syndrome, not a diagnosis. Symmetry, early falls, poor levodopa response, and early autonomic or cognitive involvement all point away from idiopathic Parkinson disease toward an atypical syndrome or a drug cause
qualifiers.misuse: Equated with Parkinson disease, so a reversible drug-induced cause continues unrecognised

qualifiers.name: Levodopa-responsive
qualifiers.definition: Meaningful and sustained improvement in motor features with adequate levodopa
qualifiers.established: A documented trial at adequate dose and duration, judged on objective motor measures rather than impression
qualifiers.example: levodopa-responsive parkinsonism → Parkinson disease
qualifiers.shift: Responsiveness supports idiopathic Parkinson disease, and a poor response after an adequate trial is one of the strongest pointers toward an atypical parkinsonian syndrome
qualifiers.misuse: Declared after an inadequate dose or too short a trial, which mislabels treatable disease as atypical

qualifiers.name: Anterograde amnesia
qualifiers.definition: Inability to form new memories after the onset of the insult
qualifiers.established: Test recall of three words at five minutes; check orientation to time repeatedly
qualifiers.associated: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, hippocampal injury, herpes encephalitis, transient global amnesia, benzodiazepines
qualifiers.example: anterograde amnesia with confabulation → Korsakoff syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Localises to the hippocampal and diencephalic memory circuit. Isolated anterograde amnesia with preserved attention and no other deficit is a focal memory problem rather than a global encephalopathy
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with inattention; a patient who cannot attend cannot register, which is a different mechanism

qualifiers.name: Confabulation
qualifiers.definition: Production of fabricated or distorted memories without intent to deceive
qualifiers.established: Ask about recent events and check answers against a collateral source
qualifiers.associated: Korsakoff syndrome, frontal lobe injury, dementia
qualifiers.example: confabulation with anterograde amnesia → Korsakoff syndrome
qualifiers.shift: The patient is not lying; they are filling a gap. With anterograde amnesia and a thiamine-deficient context this completes Korsakoff syndrome, the largely irreversible sequel of untreated Wernicke encephalopathy
qualifiers.misuse: Interpreted as dishonesty or as delusion, both of which misdirect the assessment

qualifiers.name: Paresthesia
qualifiers.definition: Abnormal spontaneous sensation: tingling, pins and needles, or burning
qualifiers.established: Map the distribution and ask whether it follows a nerve, a root, a glove and stocking pattern, or a level
qualifiers.associated: Peripheral neuropathy, radiculopathy, carpal tunnel, B12 deficiency, multiple sclerosis, hypocalcaemia
qualifiers.example: perioral paresthesia with carpopedal spasm → hypocalcaemia
qualifiers.shift: Distribution localises the lesion. Glove and stocking suggests a length-dependent neuropathy, dermatomal suggests a root, and a sensory level suggests the cord and is an emergency
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded without a distribution, which discards the only information the symptom carries

qualifiers.name: Perioral paresthesia
qualifiers.definition: Tingling around the mouth and fingertips
qualifiers.established: Ask directly in any patient with tetany, hyperventilation or after neck surgery; check Chvostek and Trousseau signs
qualifiers.associated: Hypocalcaemia, respiratory alkalosis from hyperventilation, hypomagnesaemia
qualifiers.example: perioral paresthesia after thyroid surgery → post-surgical hypocalcaemia
qualifiers.shift: Highly characteristic of acute hypocalcaemia and often the first symptom, appearing before tetany or seizure. After thyroid or parathyroid surgery it demands an immediate calcium
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to anxiety and hyperventilation, which does cause it, but only after hypocalcaemia is excluded

qualifiers.name: Restricted vertical gaze
qualifiers.definition: Impaired voluntary vertical saccades, with downgaze typically affected first and most specifically
qualifiers.established: Test voluntary vertical saccades, then check whether the movement is restored by oculocephalic manoeuvre
qualifiers.associated: Progressive supranuclear palsy, dorsal midbrain syndrome, Whipple disease
qualifiers.example: parkinsonism with early falls and restricted vertical gaze → progressive supranuclear palsy
qualifiers.shift: A supranuclear palsy is overcome by the oculocephalic reflex, which localises the lesion above the nuclei. In a parkinsonian patient with early falls this is the finding that separates PSP from Parkinson disease
qualifiers.misuse: Not tested, because vertical gaze is often omitted from a routine cranial nerve examination

qualifiers.name: Autonomic hyperactivity
qualifiers.definition: Sympathetic overdrive: tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, diaphoresis, mydriasis
qualifiers.established: Serial vital signs alongside the neurological examination; look for the pattern rather than any single value
qualifiers.associated: Alcohol withdrawal, serotonin syndrome, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, thyroid storm, phaeochromocytoma, sympathomimetic toxicity
qualifiers.example: autonomic hyperactivity with clonus and agitation → serotonin syndrome
qualifiers.shift: The accompanying neuromuscular sign discriminates: clonus and hyperreflexia suggest serotonin syndrome, lead-pipe rigidity suggests neuroleptic malignant syndrome, and tremor with a time course after the last drink suggests withdrawal
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to pain or anxiety, so a toxidrome with a specific antidote is treated as agitation

qualifiers.name: Risus sardonicus
qualifiers.definition: Sustained spasm of the facial muscles producing a fixed grimace
qualifiers.established: Observe the face; the finding is sustained rather than intermittent
qualifiers.example: risus sardonicus with trismus → tetanus
qualifiers.shift: With trismus and opisthotonus in an unimmunised patient this is close to diagnostic of tetanus, which is a clinical diagnosis because cultures are usually negative
qualifiers.misuse: Waited on; by the time the classic facies appears the disease is advanced, and trismus alone should prompt the diagnosis

qualifiers.name: Quadriparesis
qualifiers.definition: Weakness of all four limbs
qualifiers.established: Assess power in all four limbs, then look for a sensory level and for cranial nerve involvement
qualifiers.associated: Cervical cord lesion, Guillain-Barre syndrome, osmotic demyelination, botulism, periodic paralysis
qualifiers.example: quadriparesis with pseudobulbar palsy days after rapid sodium correction → osmotic demyelination
qualifiers.shift: The level matters. A sensory level suggests the cord, ascending areflexic weakness suggests Guillain-Barre, and descending weakness with pupils involved suggests botulism
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded without testing respiratory function; a falling vital capacity is what determines whether the airway is at risk

qualifiers.name: Pseudobulbar palsy
qualifiers.definition: Upper motor neuron weakness of the bulbar muscles, with a brisk jaw jerk and emotional lability
qualifiers.established: Test the jaw jerk, gag and tongue; the tongue is spastic and small rather than wasted and fasciculating
qualifiers.associated: Osmotic demyelination, bilateral strokes, motor neuron disease, multiple sclerosis
qualifiers.example: quadriparesis with pseudobulbar palsy → osmotic demyelination syndrome
qualifiers.shift: A brisk jaw jerk with a spastic tongue localises above the bulbar nuclei and implies bilateral lesions, which is a much narrower differential than unilateral weakness
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with bulbar palsy, where the tongue is wasted and fasciculating and the jaw jerk is absent, which localises to the nuclei themselves

qualifiers.name: With aura
qualifiers.definition: A reversible focal neurologic disturbance preceding or accompanying headache, typically visual, sensory or speech, spreading gradually over 5 minutes or more with each symptom lasting 5 to 60 minutes
qualifiers.established: Ask what happened before the pain, how it spread, and how long it lasted; aura evolves rather than appearing instantly
qualifiers.example: visual aura spreading over minutes then headache → migraine with aura
qualifiers.shift: Gradual evolution with full recovery favours aura, while a deficit maximal at onset favours a transient ischaemic attack. The distinction is useful rather than absolute: a minority of TIAs stutter, and late-onset aura without headache in a patient with vascular risk still warrants stroke workup. Aura also carries a modest ischaemic stroke risk that affects contraception counselling
qualifiers.misuse: Any visual symptom called aura; a deficit maximal at onset is vascular until proven otherwise

qualifiers.name: Command hallucination
qualifiers.definition: A hallucinated voice instructing the patient to perform an action
qualifiers.established: Ask directly whether the voices tell them to do things, what they say, and whether they feel compelled to obey
qualifiers.associated: Schizophrenia-spectrum illness, psychotic depression, mania, substance-induced psychosis
qualifiers.example: command hallucinations to harm oneself → acute risk requiring containment
qualifiers.shift: Does not change the diagnosis but changes the disposition. Commands to harm self or others, particularly when the patient feels compelled or has previously complied, materially raise acute risk
qualifiers.misuse: Not asked about, because the question feels intrusive. It is among the most safety-relevant questions in a psychotic presentation, with risk rising most when the patient has previously complied, the voice is familiar, or a congruent delusion accompanies it

qualifiers.name: Psychotic
qualifiers.definition: Loss of contact with reality: delusions, hallucinations, or markedly impaired reality testing
qualifiers.established: Mental state examination; establish whether insight into the unreality of the experience is retained
qualifiers.associated: Schizophrenia-spectrum illness, mood episodes with psychotic features, delirium, substance-induced states, neurologic disease
qualifiers.example: psychotic features in a depressive episode → psychotic depression
qualifiers.shift: Presence or absence changes treatment more than diagnosis: psychotic features in a mood episode call for an antipsychotic alongside the mood treatment, and psychosis with fluctuating attention is delirium until proven otherwise
qualifiers.misuse: Applied to unusual or culturally unfamiliar beliefs; a belief shared by a patient's community is not a delusion

qualifiers.name: Manic episode
qualifiers.definition: At least one week of elevated or irritable mood with increased activity or energy, causing marked impairment or requiring admission
qualifiers.established: Collateral history is essential, since insight is characteristically lost; establish duration and functional impact
qualifiers.associated: Bipolar I disorder, substance-induced mania, secondary mania from steroids or neurologic disease
qualifiers.example: one week of elevated mood with reduced sleep and grandiosity → bipolar I disorder
qualifiers.shift: Duration and severity separate this from hypomania and define bipolar I. Marked impairment, psychosis or the need for admission all indicate mania rather than hypomania
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed from the patient alone; manic patients frequently do not experience the episode as abnormal

qualifiers.name: Hypomanic episode
qualifiers.definition: At least four days of elevated or irritable mood with increased activity, clearly a change from baseline but without marked impairment, psychosis or admission
qualifiers.established: Collateral history; ask specifically about periods of reduced sleep with preserved or increased energy
qualifiers.example: four days of elevated mood without impairment, in a patient with a past major depressive episode → bipolar II disorder
qualifiers.shift: Bipolar II requires a hypomanic episode PLUS a major depressive episode, with no manic episode ever; hypomania alone is other specified bipolar disorder. It changes antidepressant strategy, since unopposed antidepressants can precipitate switching. It is routinely missed because patients present in the depressed phase and rarely volunteer the highs
qualifiers.misuse: Missed by not asking; the depressed phase is what brings people in, so hypomania must be sought

qualifiers.name: Intoxication
qualifiers.definition: A reversible syndrome caused by recent ingestion of a substance
qualifiers.established: Timeline of exposure, toxidrome-directed examination, targeted screening
qualifiers.example: agitation and mydriasis after stimulant use → sympathomimetic intoxication
qualifiers.shift: Distinguished from withdrawal by direction: intoxication follows exposure, withdrawal follows its removal, and the two produce nearly opposite autonomic pictures for the same drug class
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed from a positive drug screen, which reports exposure over days rather than current effect

qualifiers.name: Withdrawal
qualifiers.definition: A syndrome following reduction or cessation of a substance on which the patient is physiologically dependent
qualifiers.established: Establish the time of last use against symptom onset; the latency is class-specific
qualifiers.example: delirium with autonomic hyperactivity 48 to 96 hours after the last drink → delirium tremens
qualifiers.shift: Latency localises the drug: alcohol withdrawal begins within 6 to 12 hours and peaks at 24 to 48 hours, with seizures at 12 to 48 hours and delirium tremens at 48 to 96 hours; opioid withdrawal begins within a day; benzodiazepine withdrawal can be delayed more than a week with long-acting agents
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to intoxication. Withdrawal from alcohol and benzodiazepines is directly life-threatening; opioid withdrawal is rarely fatal in itself but can kill through dehydration and electrolyte loss if fluids are not replaced

qualifiers.name: Monoarticular
qualifiers.definition: One joint
qualifiers.established: Joint-by-joint examination, then arthrocentesis
qualifiers.example: acutely hot single joint → septic arthritis
qualifiers.shift: An acutely hot single joint is septic until arthrocentesis proves otherwise. This qualifier alone determines that a tap is mandatory.
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as gout on clinical grounds without a tap; the two coexist

qualifiers.name: Oligoarticular
qualifiers.definition: Two to four joints
qualifiers.established: Count and map the involved joints
qualifiers.example: asymmetric lower limb oligoarthritis → reactive arthritis
qualifiers.shift: Asymmetric large-joint oligoarthritis, especially lower limb, points toward the spondyloarthritis family.

qualifiers.name: Polyarticular
qualifiers.definition: Five or more joints
qualifiers.established: Formal joint count
qualifiers.example: symmetric small-joint polyarthritis → rheumatoid arthritis
qualifiers.shift: Symmetric small-joint polyarthritis is RA-like; acute polyarthritis with a viral prodrome suggests parvovirus B19 or hepatitis.

qualifiers.name: Migratory
qualifiers.definition: Moves from joint to joint, leaving resolved joints behind
qualifiers.established: Sequential history of joints involved and resolved
qualifiers.example: migratory arthritis → acute rheumatic fever
qualifiers.shift: A short and specific differential. Should prompt questions about pharyngitis, sexual history, and tick exposure.
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded as polyarthritis because the sequence is never asked for

qualifiers.name: Additive
qualifiers.definition: New joints accumulate while earlier ones stay involved
qualifiers.established: History of joints accumulating without earlier ones resolving
qualifiers.example: additive polyarthritis → rheumatoid arthritis
qualifiers.shift: The RA pattern; separates it from the migratory pattern above.

qualifiers.name: Palindromic
qualifiers.definition: Recurrent attacks with complete resolution between
qualifiers.established: History of attacks with complete normality between
qualifiers.example: palindromic joint swelling → evolving rheumatoid arthritis
qualifiers.shift: Complete normality between attacks. A substantial fraction evolve into RA, so anti-CCP testing is worthwhile.

qualifiers.name: Inflammatory
qualifiers.definition: Morning stiffness over an hour, better with use, swelling
qualifiers.established: Duration of morning stiffness, improvement with exercise, night pain, age at onset
qualifiers.example: inflammatory back pain → axial spondyloarthritis
qualifiers.shift: The single most useful discriminator in rheumatology. Inflammatory back pain in a patient under 45 with insidious onset and night pain opens the axial spondyloarthritis pathway.

qualifiers.name: Mechanical
qualifiers.definition: Worse with use, better with rest, brief stiffness
qualifiers.established: History of worsening with use and relief with rest
qualifiers.example: mechanical knee pain → osteoarthritis
qualifiers.shift: The mirror image of inflammatory. Argues against systemic autoimmune disease and against an urgent serologic workup.

qualifiers.name: Erosive
qualifiers.definition: Bone destruction at joint margins
qualifiers.established: Plain radiographs or ultrasound of hands and feet
qualifiers.example: marginal erosions → rheumatoid arthritis
qualifiers.shift: Evidence of structural damage. Escalates urgency of disease-modifying therapy and argues against non-destructive arthropathies.

qualifiers.name: Nonerosive
qualifiers.definition: Inflammation without radiographic bone destruction
qualifiers.established: Radiographs showing deformity without erosion
qualifiers.example: deforming nonerosive arthropathy → lupus (Jaccoud arthropathy)
qualifiers.shift: Deformity without erosion is characteristic of lupus and separates it from RA, which erodes.

qualifiers.name: Enthesitis
qualifiers.definition: Inflammation where tendon or ligament inserts into bone
qualifiers.established: Palpation of tendon insertions, notably Achilles and plantar fascia
qualifiers.example: Achilles enthesitis → spondyloarthritis
qualifiers.shift: Close to specific for the spondyloarthritis family. Insertional heel pain or plantar fascia tenderness in a young patient with back pain is a strong clue.

qualifiers.name: Dactylitis
qualifiers.definition: Uniform swelling of an entire digit
qualifiers.established: Inspection for uniform swelling across the whole digit
qualifiers.associated: Psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis, sarcoid, sickle cell
qualifiers.example: sausage digit → psoriatic arthritis
qualifiers.shift: Swelling across joints and tendon sheaths rather than confined to a joint line. Strongly suggests psoriatic or reactive arthritis.
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded as arthritis of the individual joints

qualifiers.name: Seropositive
qualifiers.definition: Autoantibodies present
qualifiers.established: Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP testing
qualifiers.example: anti-CCP positive polyarthritis → erosive rheumatoid arthritis
qualifiers.shift: Anti-CCP in particular predicts erosive disease and a worse trajectory, which justifies earlier and more aggressive therapy.

qualifiers.name: Seronegative
qualifiers.definition: Characteristic autoantibodies absent
qualifiers.established: Negative RF and anti-CCP in the presence of the clinical syndrome
qualifiers.example: seronegative inflammatory arthritis → spondyloarthritis
qualifiers.shift: Does not exclude the disease. In spondyloarthritis, seronegativity is expected and the term denotes a family of conditions rather than a failed test.
qualifiers.misuse: Used to exclude disease; seronegativity is expected in spondyloarthritis

qualifiers.name: Gelling
qualifiers.definition: Stiffness after a period of inactivity that eases with movement
qualifiers.established: Ask how long stiffness lasts after sitting
qualifiers.example: gelling after inactivity → osteoarthritis
qualifiers.shift: Brief gelling of minutes suits osteoarthritis; prolonged morning stiffness beyond an hour suits inflammatory disease.

qualifiers.name: DIP-sparing
qualifiers.definition: Distal interphalangeal joints not involved
qualifiers.established: Examine the distal interphalangeal joints specifically
qualifiers.example: DIP-sparing polyarthritis → rheumatoid arthritis
qualifiers.shift: A clean discriminator. RA spares the DIPs; osteoarthritis and psoriatic arthritis characteristically involve them.

qualifiers.name: Sicca
qualifiers.definition: Dryness of eyes and mouth
qualifiers.established: Ask about dry eyes and mouth; Schirmer test if needed
qualifiers.example: sicca symptoms → Sjögren syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Prompts anti-Ro and anti-La testing and raises the associated risks of renal tubular acidosis and lymphoma.

qualifiers.name: Large-vessel vasculitis
qualifiers.definition: Aorta and its major branches
qualifiers.established: Four-limb blood pressures, bruits, and vascular imaging
qualifiers.example: limb claudication with blood pressure discrepancy → Takayasu arteritis
qualifiers.shift: Predicts limb claudication, bruits, blood pressure discrepancies, and aortic complications, and points to imaging of the aorta rather than tissue biopsy of small vessels.

qualifiers.name: Medium-vessel vasculitis
qualifiers.definition: Main visceral arteries and their branches
qualifiers.established: Angiography or biopsy of an affected organ
qualifiers.example: renal microaneurysms with mononeuritis → polyarteritis nodosa
qualifiers.shift: Predicts aneurysms, infarcts, and mononeuritis multiplex. Notably spares glomeruli, so glomerulonephritis argues against classic polyarteritis nodosa.
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed when glomerulonephritis is present, which argues against it

qualifiers.name: Small-vessel vasculitis
qualifiers.definition: Arterioles, capillaries, venules
qualifiers.established: Skin or renal biopsy plus ANCA serology
qualifiers.example: palpable purpura with hematuria → ANCA-associated vasculitis
qualifiers.shift: Predicts palpable purpura, glomerulonephritis, and alveolar hemorrhage. The pulmonary-renal syndrome lives here.

qualifiers.name: Pauci-immune
qualifiers.definition: Little or no immune complex deposition on immunofluorescence
qualifiers.established: Renal biopsy with immunofluorescence
qualifiers.example: pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis → ANCA vasculitis
qualifiers.shift: Separates ANCA vasculitis from immune complex disease and from anti-GBM disease on the same biopsy, which drives entirely different treatment.

qualifiers.name: Low complement
qualifiers.definition: Reduced C3 and C4 from consumption
qualifiers.established: Serum C3 and C4
qualifiers.associated: Lupus nephritis, post-infectious GN, cryoglobulinemia, endocarditis
qualifiers.example: low C3 and C4 with nephritis → lupus nephritis
qualifiers.shift: One of the most efficient discriminators in nephritis. Low complement narrows a long differential to a short one; normal complement points elsewhere, including ANCA vasculitis and IgA nephropathy.

qualifiers.name: Negatively birefringent
qualifiers.definition: Yellow when parallel to the compensator axis
qualifiers.established: Polarized light microscopy of synovial fluid
qualifiers.example: negatively birefringent needles → gout
qualifiers.shift: Definitive for gout on synovial fluid. Note that crystals and infection can coexist, so their presence does not exclude septic arthritis.
qualifiers.misuse: Crystals do not exclude coexisting infection; always send fluid for culture too

qualifiers.name: Positively birefringent
qualifiers.definition: Blue when parallel to the compensator axis
qualifiers.established: Polarized light microscopy of synovial fluid
qualifiers.example: positively birefringent rhomboids → calcium pyrophosphate deposition
qualifiers.shift: Identifies calcium pyrophosphate deposition, which should prompt evaluation for hemochromatosis, hyperparathyroidism, and hypomagnesemia in younger patients.
qualifiers.misuse: Accepted as the final answer in a young patient without screening for hemochromatosis or hyperparathyroidism

qualifiers.name: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis
qualifiers.definition: Skin thickening distal to elbows and knees, plus face
qualifiers.established: Map the proximal extent of skin thickening
qualifiers.example: limited cutaneous sclerosis → pulmonary arterial hypertension risk
qualifiers.shift: Predicts pulmonary arterial hypertension as the dominant late risk and a lower risk of scleroderma renal crisis.

qualifiers.name: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis
qualifiers.definition: Skin thickening proximal to elbows and knees, including trunk
qualifiers.established: Map skin involvement proximal to elbows and knees or on the trunk
qualifiers.example: diffuse cutaneous sclerosis → scleroderma renal crisis risk
qualifiers.shift: Predicts interstitial lung disease and scleroderma renal crisis, and warrants blood pressure surveillance and early lung screening.
qualifiers.misuse: Blood pressure not monitored, which is how renal crisis is missed

qualifiers.name: Nailfold capillary abnormality
qualifiers.definition: Dilated loops and dropout on capillaroscopy
qualifiers.established: Dermatoscope or ophthalmoscope at the cuticle
qualifiers.example: abnormal nailfold capillaries → secondary Raynaud from systemic sclerosis
qualifiers.shift: Separates secondary from primary Raynaud phenomenon at the bedside with a simple magnifier, and predicts progression to a connective tissue disease.

qualifiers.name: Tophaceous
qualifiers.definition: Palpable deposits of urate in soft tissue
qualifiers.established: Inspection and palpation of ears, elbows, and digits
qualifiers.example: tophi over the helix and olecranon → chronic untreated gout
qualifiers.shift: Indicates a large total urate burden, mandates urate-lowering therapy, and requires a lower serum urate target than non-tophaceous disease.

qualifiers.name: Degenerative
qualifiers.definition: Caused by progressive structural deterioration
qualifiers.established: Radiographs showing joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis
qualifiers.example: degenerative changes on radiograph → osteoarthritis
qualifiers.shift: Points away from inflammatory arthropathy. Note that degenerative change is near-universal with age, so its presence does not explain a patient's pain by itself
qualifiers.misuse: Radiographic degeneration reported as the cause of symptoms; prevalence in asymptomatic adults is very high

qualifiers.name: Arthritis
qualifiers.definition: Joint inflammation with swelling, warmth, tenderness and restricted movement
qualifiers.established: Distinguish true synovitis from arthralgia by finding swelling and warmth, not just pain
qualifiers.associated: Rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, gout, septic arthritis, reactive arthritis, lupus, Still disease
qualifiers.example: arthritis with quotidian fever and an evanescent rash → adult-onset Still disease
qualifiers.shift: Objective synovitis, as opposed to joint pain alone, narrows the differential sharply toward inflammatory disease. Number of joints, symmetry and pattern then do the rest
qualifiers.misuse: Used interchangeably with arthralgia. Pain without swelling is arthralgia and has a much broader and more benign differential

qualifiers.name: Nasal chondritis
qualifiers.definition: Inflammation of the cartilage of the nose, sparing the bony bridge
qualifiers.established: Inspect and gently palpate the cartilaginous nose; look for a saddle deformity
qualifiers.example: nasal chondritis with airway involvement → relapsing polychondritis
qualifiers.shift: Cartilage-specific inflammation that spares bone is a short differential. With auricular chondritis sparing the lobe, which contains no cartilage, it is close to characteristic of relapsing polychondritis
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with cellulitis; the sparing of the non-cartilaginous ear lobe is the distinguishing observation

qualifiers.name: Salivary gland enlargement
qualifiers.definition: Persistent swelling of the parotid or submandibular glands
qualifiers.established: Palpate both glands, express the ducts, and assess for dry mouth and eyes
qualifiers.associated: Sjogren syndrome, IgG4-related disease, sarcoidosis, lymphoma, mumps, sialolithiasis
qualifiers.example: salivary gland enlargement with raised IgG4 → IgG4-related disease
qualifiers.shift: Bilateral persistent painless enlargement suggests an infiltrative or autoimmune process rather than infection. In Sjogren it carries a lifelong lymphoma risk, so new asymmetry in a known patient needs tissue
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to mumps in an adult, where the differential is quite different

qualifiers.name: Pathergy positive
qualifiers.definition: A pustule forming at the site of minor skin trauma within 24 to 48 hours
qualifiers.established: Sterile needle prick to the forearm, read at 24 to 48 hours
qualifiers.associated: Behcet disease, pyoderma gangrenosum, Sweet syndrome
qualifiers.example: oral and genital ulceration with pathergy → Behcet disease
qualifiers.shift: Reflects neutrophilic hyperreactivity, supports Behcet disease in the right setting, and warns against surgery in pyoderma gangrenosum where trauma enlarges the lesion
qualifiers.misuse: Read too early; the reaction takes at least 24 hours to develop

qualifiers.name: Abnormal nailfold capillaries
qualifiers.definition: Dilated, dropped out or haemorrhagic capillary loops at the nailfold
qualifiers.established: Dermatoscope or ophthalmoscope at high plus power with a drop of oil at the nailfold
qualifiers.associated: Systemic sclerosis, dermatomyositis, mixed connective tissue disease
qualifiers.example: Raynaud with abnormal nailfold capillaries → systemic sclerosis
qualifiers.shift: A valuable bedside test which, alongside autoantibody testing, helps separate primary from secondary Raynaud phenomenon, and abnormality can precede other features by years. Normal capillaries with a negative ANA is the reassuring combination, not capillaroscopy alone
qualifiers.misuse: Not performed, because it is assumed to need specialist equipment when an ophthalmoscope will do

qualifiers.name: Mucosal involvement
qualifiers.definition: Erosion or ulceration of mucous membranes: oral, ocular, genital
qualifiers.established: Inspect mouth, conjunctivae and genitalia in any significant rash
qualifiers.associated: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, pemphigus vulgaris, Behcet disease, mucous membrane pemphigoid
qualifiers.example: dusky macules with mucosal involvement at two sites → Stevens-Johnson syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Two or more mucosal sites are involved in over 90% of cases and are highly characteristic, separating this from lesser drug eruptions and changing disposition to a burns unit. The spectrum itself is formally classified by extent of epidermal detachment
qualifiers.misuse: Mucosae not examined in a patient with a rash, which is how the diagnosis is delayed

qualifiers.name: Articular
qualifiers.definition: Arising from the joint itself rather than the surrounding structures
qualifiers.established: Passive movement hurts in all planes and swelling is within the joint line
qualifiers.associated: Osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, septic arthritis
qualifiers.example: pain on passive movement in every plane with joint line swelling → articular
qualifiers.shift: Separates true joint disease from the far commoner periarticular problems, which changes both the differential and whether aspiration is indicated. Passive pain in all planes is the most useful bedside discriminator, though a large effusion or capsular periarticular disease can blur it
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed from where the patient points; periarticular pain is frequently reported as joint pain

qualifiers.name: Periarticular
qualifiers.definition: Arising from the structures around a joint: tendon, bursa, enthesis or muscle
qualifiers.established: Passive movement is comparatively preserved while resisted movement in one specific direction reproduces the pain
qualifiers.example: pain on resisted abduction with preserved passive range → rotator cuff tendinopathy
qualifiers.shift: Far more common than true arthritis and treated entirely differently. Point tenderness away from the joint line with pain in one direction of resisted movement identifies it in seconds
qualifiers.misuse: Investigated with joint imaging and aspiration, which is invasive and answers a question that was not being asked

qualifiers.name: Blanching
qualifiers.definition: Pales with pressure
qualifiers.established: Press with a glass slide or fingertip
qualifiers.example: blanching maculopapular rash → viral exanthem
qualifiers.shift: Vasodilation rather than extravasation. Generally reassuring and moves away from vasculitis and thrombocytopenia.

qualifiers.name: Nonblanching
qualifiers.definition: Persists with pressure
qualifiers.established: Glass slide or diascopy over the lesion
qualifiers.example: nonblanching petechial rash with fever → meningococcemia
qualifiers.shift: The most urgent qualifier in dermatology. With fever it triggers immediate empiric therapy for meningococcemia; otherwise it directs toward thrombocytopenia or vasculitis.
qualifiers.misuse: Not tested at all; the single most important bedside maneuver in a febrile rash

qualifiers.name: Macular
qualifiers.definition: Flat
qualifiers.established: Inspection and palpation for elevation
qualifiers.example: macular eruption → drug or viral exanthem
qualifiers.shift: Flat lesions imply a process in the epidermis or dermis without significant infiltrate or fluid.

qualifiers.name: Papular
qualifiers.definition: Raised, solid, small
qualifiers.established: Palpation confirming raised solid lesions
qualifiers.example: papular eruption → arthropod bites or drug eruption
qualifiers.shift: Implies a dermal cellular infiltrate.

qualifiers.name: Maculopapular
qualifiers.definition: Both flat and raised
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus timing relative to drug exposure
qualifiers.example: maculopapular eruption after a new drug → drug exanthem
qualifiers.shift: The most common inpatient rash. The key branch point is timing relative to drug exposure and the presence of fever, eosinophilia, or mucosal involvement.
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed benign without checking for eosinophilia, mucosal involvement, or organ dysfunction

qualifiers.name: Vesicular
qualifiers.definition: Small fluid-filled
qualifiers.established: Inspection; PCR of vesicle fluid if uncertain
qualifiers.example: grouped vesicles on an erythematous base → herpes simplex or zoster
qualifiers.shift: Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base is herpetic. Distribution then separates zoster from disseminated infection.

qualifiers.name: Bullous
qualifiers.definition: Large fluid-filled
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus Nikolsky testing and mucosal examination
qualifiers.example: tense bullae in an elderly patient → bullous pemphigoid
qualifiers.shift: Raises the blistering emergencies. Mucosal involvement plus a positive Nikolsky sign is a dermatologic emergency.

qualifiers.name: Pustular
qualifiers.definition: Pus-filled
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus culture to establish sterility
qualifiers.example: sterile pustules → acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
qualifiers.shift: Neutrophilic. Sterile pustules suggest pustular psoriasis or AGEP rather than infection.

qualifiers.name: Petechial
qualifiers.definition: Pinpoint nonblanching hemorrhages
qualifiers.established: Diascopy plus urgent platelet count
qualifiers.example: petechiae → thrombocytopenia
qualifiers.shift: Mandates an immediate platelet count and, with fever, empiric antibiotics before results.

qualifiers.name: Purpuric
qualifiers.definition: Larger nonblanching hemorrhagic lesions
qualifiers.established: Diascopy and palpation for elevation
qualifiers.example: purpuric lesions → vasculitis or coagulopathy
qualifiers.shift: Palpable purpura specifically indicates small-vessel vasculitis and warrants a search for renal and pulmonary involvement.

qualifiers.name: Palpable purpura
qualifiers.definition: Purpura raised above the skin surface
qualifiers.established: Close the eyes and palpate; the elevation is the finding
qualifiers.example: palpable purpura → small-vessel vasculitis
qualifiers.shift: The tactile quality is the diagnosis. Palpability implies inflammatory vessel wall infiltration rather than simple extravasation.
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed by sight alone, which cannot detect palpability

qualifiers.name: Urticarial
qualifiers.definition: Transient migratory wheals
qualifiers.established: Circle a lesion and reassess after 24 hours
qualifiers.example: wheals resolving within 24 hours → ordinary urticaria
qualifiers.shift: Individual lesions lasting under 24 hours is ordinary urticaria; lesions lasting longer, bruising, or burning rather than itching suggests urticarial vasculitis.
qualifiers.misuse: Persistent lesions called urticaria; longer than a day suggests urticarial vasculitis

qualifiers.name: Targetoid
qualifiers.definition: Concentric rings
qualifiers.established: Inspection for concentric zones
qualifiers.example: three-zone target lesions on the palms → erythema multiforme
qualifiers.shift: True three-zone targets on acral surfaces suggest erythema multiforme, most often HSV-driven.

qualifiers.name: Annular
qualifiers.definition: Ring-shaped with central clearing
qualifiers.established: Inspection of the border plus skin scraping for KOH
qualifiers.example: annular scaling plaque with central clearing → tinea corporis
qualifiers.shift: A scaling advancing border suggests dermatophyte; a non-scaling expanding ring after tick exposure suggests erythema migrans.
qualifiers.misuse: Treated with topical steroid, which produces tinea incognito

qualifiers.name: Reticular
qualifiers.definition: Net-like
qualifiers.established: Inspection with attention to symmetry and completeness of the net
qualifiers.example: reticular mottling → livedo reticularis
qualifiers.shift: Implies impaired dermal microcirculation and prompts consideration of antiphospholipid syndrome, vasculitis, and emboli.

qualifiers.name: Confluent
qualifiers.definition: Lesions merge
qualifiers.established: Serial inspection documenting merging
qualifiers.example: confluent morbilliform eruption → measles or drug rash
qualifiers.shift: Progression from discrete to confluent generally indicates a worsening or evolving eruption.

qualifiers.name: Acral
qualifiers.definition: Hands, feet, and distal extremities
qualifiers.established: Deliberately examine palms and soles
qualifiers.associated: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease, secondary syphilis, endocarditis lesions
qualifiers.example: palmar and plantar rash → secondary syphilis
