qualifiers.example: resistant hypertension with hypokalaemia → primary aldosteronism
qualifiers.shift: Almost always primary, but resistance to three agents, onset under 30 or over 55, or hypokalaemia should trigger a search for a secondary cause
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed on a single reading with the wrong cuff size, which overestimates in large arms

qualifiers.name: Hypoalbuminaemia
qualifiers.definition: Serum albumin below the reference range
qualifiers.established: Serum albumin, interpreted alongside inflammatory markers and urinary protein
qualifiers.associated: Nephrotic syndrome, cirrhosis, malnutrition, protein-losing enteropathy, acute inflammation
qualifiers.example: hypoalbuminaemia with nephrotic-range proteinuria → nephrotic syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Distinguish loss from underproduction from redistribution. In acute illness albumin falls as a negative acute phase reactant and reflects inflammation rather than nutrition
qualifiers.misuse: Read as a nutritional marker in acute illness, where it mostly measures how sick the patient is

qualifiers.name: Coagulopathy
qualifiers.definition: Impaired clot formation, reflected in prolonged clotting times or a low fibrinogen
qualifiers.established: Prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen, platelet count; a mixing study separates factor deficiency from an inhibitor
qualifiers.associated: Liver disease, DIC, vitamin K deficiency, anticoagulants, massive transfusion
qualifiers.example: coagulopathy with a low fibrinogen and schistocytes → disseminated intravascular coagulation
qualifiers.shift: Which times are prolonged localizes the problem to the extrinsic, intrinsic, or common pathway, and a falling fibrinogen with thrombocytopenia points at consumption rather than synthetic failure
qualifiers.misuse: Prolonged times in liver disease read as a bleeding tendency; the balanced loss of anticoagulant factors means these patients are not reliably auto-anticoagulated

qualifiers.name: Rhabdomyolysis
qualifiers.definition: Skeletal muscle breakdown releasing myoglobin, potassium and phosphate into the circulation
qualifiers.established: Creatine kinase, typically more than five times the upper limit; urine dipstick positive for blood with no red cells on microscopy
qualifiers.associated: Crush injury, prolonged immobility, statins, seizures, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, exertional heat illness
qualifiers.example: rhabdomyolysis with hyperkalaemia → crush injury
qualifiers.shift: Explains acute kidney injury, hyperkalaemia, hypocalcaemia and a raised phosphate in one mechanism, and the dipstick-microscopy mismatch is the clue that costs nothing
qualifiers.misuse: Excluded on a normal creatinine; kidney injury is a complication rather than a requirement

qualifiers.name: Night sweats
qualifiers.definition: Drenching sweats during sleep, sufficient to require a change of bedding
qualifiers.established: Ask specifically about drenching and bedding changes rather than feeling warm
qualifiers.associated: Lymphoma, tuberculosis, endocarditis, HIV, menopause, hyperthyroidism
qualifiers.example: night sweats with weight loss and lymphadenopathy → lymphoma
qualifiers.shift: Only useful when drenching. With weight loss and fever it forms the B symptom triad and raises lymphoma and chronic infection substantially
qualifiers.misuse: Any nocturnal warmth accepted, which makes an otherwise useful symptom meaningless

qualifiers.name: Unintentional weight loss
qualifiers.definition: Loss of more than five percent of body weight over six to twelve months without trying
qualifiers.established: Corroborate against recorded weights or clothing fit rather than estimate
qualifiers.associated: Malignancy, tuberculosis, HIV, hyperthyroidism, depression, malabsorption
qualifiers.example: unintentional weight loss with night sweats → lymphoma
qualifiers.shift: One of the highest-yield red flags in general medicine. Documented rather than reported loss roughly doubles the probability of a serious underlying cause
qualifiers.misuse: Accepted on report alone; recalled weight loss is unreliable and frequently overstated

qualifiers.name: Morning stiffness
qualifiers.definition: Joint stiffness on waking that improves with movement
qualifiers.established: Ask how long it lasts before near-normal function returns
qualifiers.example: morning stiffness over an hour → rheumatoid arthritis
qualifiers.shift: Duration is the discriminator. More than an hour suggests inflammatory arthritis, while brief stiffness that returns after rest suggests osteoarthritis
qualifiers.misuse: Duration not asked; without it the symptom does not separate the two groups it exists to separate

qualifiers.name: Injury inconsistent with the mechanism
qualifiers.definition: Injuries whose pattern, distribution, or severity does not fit the history given
qualifiers.established: Compare the described mechanism against the injury pattern and the patient's developmental stage or functional capacity; interview separately where safe
qualifiers.associated: Non-accidental injury in children, elder mistreatment, intimate partner violence
qualifiers.example: injuries inconsistent with the mechanism given → non-accidental injury
qualifiers.shift: The single most important safeguarding qualifier. A bruise on a child who is not yet cruising, a spiral long bone fracture in a non-ambulant patient, or a history that changes between tellings each mandate escalation rather than reassurance
qualifiers.misuse: Explained away by an apparently plausible caregiver account; the inconsistency itself is the finding and it obliges a safeguarding referral

qualifiers.name: Injuries at varying stages of healing
qualifiers.definition: Coexisting injuries of visibly different ages
qualifiers.established: Full skin survey with documentation; skeletal survey in children where indicated
qualifiers.associated: Non-accidental injury, elder mistreatment, repeated falls
qualifiers.example: injuries at varying stages of healing → non-accidental injury
qualifiers.shift: Implies repeated events over time rather than a single accident, which changes the question from how this happened to how long it has been happening
qualifiers.misuse: Bruise ageing by colour, which is unreliable; the finding rests on clearly different stages, not precise dating

qualifiers.name: Delayed presentation
qualifiers.definition: A substantial and unexplained interval between an injury or symptom onset and seeking care
qualifiers.established: Establish the time of onset and the time of presentation separately, and ask what prompted attendance now
qualifiers.associated: Non-accidental injury, elder mistreatment, barriers to access, fear, cognitive impairment
qualifiers.example: delayed presentation with inconsistent history → elder mistreatment
qualifiers.shift: In a safeguarding context this is corroborating rather than diagnostic, and it has innocent explanations including cost, transport, and fear, so it must be weighed rather than assumed
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as evidence of neglect without exploring access barriers, which penalizes the poorest patients

qualifiers.name: Caregiver control of the interview
qualifiers.definition: A caregiver answering for the patient, refusing to leave, or correcting the patient's account
qualifiers.established: Note who speaks; attempt to interview the patient alone as a matter of routine
qualifiers.associated: Elder mistreatment, intimate partner violence, coercive control
qualifiers.example: caregiver control of the interview → elder mistreatment
qualifiers.shift: A behavioural red flag that is free to observe and easily missed. Its value is that it prompts a separate interview, which is where disclosure actually happens
qualifiers.misuse: Read as devotion; an attentive relative and a controlling one look identical until the patient is seen alone

qualifiers.name: Malnutrition
qualifiers.definition: Deficient intake or absorption sufficient to impair function and body composition
qualifiers.established: Weight and weight trajectory, muscle and fat stores, and a validated screening tool rather than albumin
qualifiers.associated: Elder mistreatment, malabsorption, malignancy, dementia, poverty, chronic illness
qualifiers.example: malnutrition with delayed presentation → elder mistreatment
qualifiers.shift: In an older adult with a caregiver, unexplained weight loss alongside poor hygiene and missed appointments raises neglect. In isolation the differential remains broad
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed from albumin, which falls with inflammation and is a poor nutritional marker

qualifiers.name: Compensation deviating from prediction
qualifiers.definition: Measured compensation that differs from the value predicted for the primary acid-base disturbance
qualifiers.established: Apply the expected compensation formula for the primary disorder, then compare with the measured value
qualifiers.associated: Mixed acid-base disorders, salicylate toxicity, sepsis with vomiting, chronic lung disease with acute illness
qualifiers.example: compensation deviating from prediction → mixed acid-base disorder
qualifiers.shift: The only way to detect a second disturbance hiding behind the first. Compensation never fully corrects the pH and never overshoots, so an over- or under-shoot proves more than one process is present
qualifiers.misuse: Not calculated at all; without the predicted value a mixed disorder is invisible and is read as a single one

qualifiers.name: Viral prodrome
qualifiers.definition: A short nonspecific illness with fever, myalgia and coryza preceding the presenting problem
qualifiers.established: Ask directly about the days to weeks before onset; patients rarely connect the two
qualifiers.associated: Myocarditis, Guillain-Barre syndrome, immune thrombocytopenia, post-viral cerebellitis, reactive arthritis
qualifiers.example: raised troponin after a viral prodrome → acute myocarditis
qualifiers.shift: Supplies a mechanism for an otherwise unexplained presentation and shifts the differential toward post-infectious and immune-mediated disease. The latency is informative: days for direct infection, one to three weeks for immune-mediated sequelae
qualifiers.misuse: Not asked about, so the link between a trivial illness and a serious sequel is never made

qualifiers.name: Menorrhagia
qualifiers.definition: Heavy menstrual bleeding sufficient to affect quality of life or cause anaemia
qualifiers.established: Ask about flooding, clots, protection changes per hour, and iron studies
qualifiers.associated: Von Willebrand disease, platelet disorders, fibroids, anticoagulation, hypothyroidism, endometrial pathology
qualifiers.example: menorrhagia with mucocutaneous bleeding → von Willebrand disease
qualifiers.shift: In an adolescent or a woman with other mucocutaneous bleeding this is often the presenting feature of an inherited bleeding disorder, most commonly von Willebrand disease, which is frequently diagnosed years late
qualifiers.misuse: Normalised by both patient and clinician, so a treatable bleeding disorder or an iron deficiency is missed

qualifiers.name: Pregnancy loss
qualifiers.definition: Loss of pregnancy before viability, particularly when recurrent
qualifiers.established: Take an obstetric history including gestation at each loss and whether losses were early or late
qualifiers.associated: Antiphospholipid syndrome, uterine anomaly, chromosomal abnormality, thyroid and metabolic disease
qualifiers.example: recurrent pregnancy loss with arterial or venous thrombosis → antiphospholipid syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Recurrent loss, especially after the first trimester, alongside thrombosis and persistently positive antibodies, defines antiphospholipid syndrome, which changes management of any future pregnancy entirely
qualifiers.misuse: Investigated after a single early loss, where sporadic chromosomal causes dominate and testing mostly generates anxiety

qualifiers.name: Positive pregnancy test
qualifiers.definition: Detectable beta-hCG in urine or serum
qualifiers.established: Urine or serum beta-hCG in any person of childbearing potential presenting with abdominal or pelvic pain, syncope, or shock
qualifiers.associated: Intrauterine pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, gestational trophoblastic disease
qualifiers.example: positive pregnancy test with unilateral pelvic pain and no intrauterine gestation → ectopic pregnancy
qualifiers.shift: Reframes an entire abdominal or pelvic presentation. Until an intrauterine pregnancy is demonstrated, a positive test with pain or bleeding is an ectopic until proven otherwise, and rupture can present as undifferentiated shock
qualifiers.misuse: Not sent, which is the commonest reason ectopic pregnancy is missed. It must be reflexive, not conditional on the patient thinking she could be pregnant

qualifiers.name: No intrauterine gestation
qualifiers.definition: Absence of a visible intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound despite a positive beta-hCG
qualifiers.established: Transvaginal ultrasound interpreted alongside the beta-hCG level and the discriminatory zone
qualifiers.associated: Ectopic pregnancy, very early intrauterine pregnancy, complete miscarriage
qualifiers.example: positive pregnancy test with no intrauterine gestation → ectopic pregnancy
qualifiers.shift: An empty uterus above the discriminatory zone means the pregnancy is somewhere else until proven otherwise. Below that threshold the finding is uninterpretable and needs serial hCG rather than reassurance
qualifiers.misuse: Read as excluding pregnancy; it does the opposite, and a pseudogestational sac is mistaken for an intrauterine pregnancy

qualifiers.name: Fever
qualifiers.definition: A regulated rise in core temperature above 38 degrees
qualifiers.established: Measure core temperature; note the pattern and whether it is truly regulated rather than hyperthermia
qualifiers.associated: Infection, malignancy, autoimmune disease, drug reaction, thromboembolism
qualifiers.example: quotidian fever with an evanescent salmon rash → adult-onset Still disease
qualifiers.shift: Pattern occasionally helps: quotidian spikes suggest Still disease or abscess, relative bradycardia suggests typhoid or Legionella, and stepwise rise suggests enteric fever. Absence of fever does not exclude infection in the elderly or immunosuppressed
qualifiers.misuse: Absence taken as reassurance in older adults, in whom serious infection frequently presents without it

qualifiers.name: Fatigue
qualifiers.definition: Persistent tiredness disproportionate to exertion and not relieved by rest
qualifiers.established: Distinguish from sleepiness and from weakness; ask about onset, trajectory and functional impact
qualifiers.associated: Anaemia, hypothyroidism, depression, sleep apnoea, malignancy, heart failure, renal failure, chronic infection
qualifiers.example: fatigue with weight loss and night sweats → lymphoma
qualifiers.shift: Almost useless alone and quite useful in company. The accompanying features do the work, and its value lies in prompting a search for the accompanying features rather than a broad panel of tests
qualifiers.misuse: Investigated with an undirected battery of tests, which yields false positives more often than diagnoses

qualifiers.name: Headache
qualifiers.definition: Pain in the head or upper neck
qualifiers.established: Establish onset speed, worst-ever quality, positional change, and any associated neurological or systemic feature
qualifiers.associated: Migraine, tension type, subarachnoid haemorrhage, meningitis, giant cell arteritis, raised intracranial pressure
qualifiers.example: hyperacute worst-ever headache → subarachnoid haemorrhage
qualifiers.shift: Onset speed is the single most discriminating feature. Thunderclap onset is subarachnoid haemorrhage until excluded, new headache over 50 raises giant cell arteritis, and positional worsening suggests a pressure problem
qualifiers.misuse: Treated symptomatically without establishing onset speed, which is the question that separates benign from catastrophic

qualifiers.name: Abdominal pain
qualifiers.definition: Pain arising from abdominal or pelvic structures
qualifiers.established: Establish location, radiation, onset speed, relation to meals and movement, and migration
qualifiers.associated: Appendicitis, cholecystitis, pancreatitis, obstruction, perforation, ischaemia, ectopic pregnancy, aortic aneurysm
qualifiers.example: abdominal pain out of proportion to examination → acute mesenteric ischaemia
qualifiers.shift: Migration is highly informative, as in periumbilical pain moving to the right iliac fossa. Pain preceding vomiting suggests a surgical cause, and pain out of proportion to signs suggests ischaemia
qualifiers.misuse: Localised by the patient's gesture alone; visceral pain is poorly localised early and migrates as the peritoneum becomes involved

qualifiers.name: Nausea
qualifiers.definition: The sensation of impending vomiting
qualifiers.established: Ask about relation to meals, position, and associated headache or vertigo
qualifiers.associated: Gastrointestinal disease, raised intracranial pressure, metabolic derangement, pregnancy, drugs, vestibular disease
qualifiers.example: nausea with headache worse on lying flat → raised intracranial pressure
qualifiers.shift: Nonspecific but occasionally localising. Vomiting without nausea suggests a central cause, early morning vomiting suggests raised intracranial pressure, and vomiting that relieves pain suggests obstruction
qualifiers.misuse: Treated with an antiemetic before a pregnancy test in a person of childbearing potential

qualifiers.name: Hypoxemia
qualifiers.definition: Arterial oxygen tension or saturation below normal
qualifiers.established: Pulse oximetry confirmed by arterial gas; calculate the alveolar-arterial gradient
qualifiers.associated: Pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, heart failure, ARDS, shunt, hypoventilation
qualifiers.example: hypoxaemia with clear lungs and a raised A-a gradient → pulmonary embolism
qualifiers.shift: The alveolar-arterial gradient separates hypoventilation, where the gradient is normal, from shunt and dead space, where it is widened. Hypoxaemia with a clear chest radiograph is the classic embolism presentation
qualifiers.misuse: Read from oximetry alone, which is unreliable in poor perfusion, carbon monoxide poisoning and dark nail polish

qualifiers.name: Jaw claudication
qualifiers.definition: Pain in the masticatory muscles brought on by chewing and relieved by rest
qualifiers.established: Ask specifically whether the jaw tires or aches while eating; patients rarely volunteer it
qualifiers.example: new headache over 50 with jaw claudication → giant cell arteritis
qualifiers.shift: The historical feature with the highest positive likelihood ratio in giant cell arteritis, roughly 4 to 5, and the most specific symptom. Its presence justifies starting steroids before biopsy, because vision loss is irreversible and can occur within days
qualifiers.misuse: Not asked about, so the single most discriminating symptom in the syndrome goes unrecorded

qualifiers.name: Relieved by leaning forward
qualifiers.definition: Pain that eases when the patient sits up and leans forward
qualifiers.established: Ask directly, and observe the position the patient adopts spontaneously
qualifiers.example: chest pain relieved by leaning forward → acute pericarditis
qualifiers.shift: Positional relief points at an inflamed serosal surface rather than a vascular event, which is the practical distinction from myocardial infarction at the bedside
qualifiers.misuse: Not asked, though it costs one question and moves the differential substantially

qualifiers.name: Improves with exercise
qualifiers.definition: Symptoms that lessen rather than worsen with continued activity
qualifiers.established: Ask whether the first movements of the day are the worst and whether activity helps
qualifiers.associated: Inflammatory arthritis, axial spondyloarthritis, Lambert-Eaton syndrome
qualifiers.example: back pain that improves with exercise and is worse at rest → axial spondyloarthritis
qualifiers.shift: Reverses the usual mechanical pattern and is the cardinal feature of inflammatory back pain. Mechanical pain worsens with use and improves with rest; inflammatory pain does the opposite
qualifiers.misuse: Not asked, so inflammatory back pain in a young adult is managed as mechanical for years

qualifiers.name: Worse at night
qualifiers.definition: Symptoms that wake the patient or are worst in the small hours
qualifiers.established: Ask whether the symptom wakes them from sleep, not merely whether it is present at night
qualifiers.associated: Malignancy, infection, inflammatory arthritis, spinal cord compression, cluster headache
qualifiers.example: back pain worse at night with weight loss → malignant spinal cord compression
qualifiers.shift: Night pain that wakes the patient is a red flag in back pain and bone pain, pointing at malignancy or infection rather than a mechanical cause
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded when the patient merely notices it at night, which is not the same as being woken by it

qualifiers.name: Solid-food dysphagia
qualifiers.definition: Difficulty swallowing solids, with liquids initially tolerated
qualifiers.established: Establish whether solids alone or both solids and liquids are affected, and whether it is progressive
qualifiers.associated: Oesophageal carcinoma, peptic stricture, eosinophilic oesophagitis, Schatzki ring
qualifiers.example: progressive solid-food dysphagia with weight loss → oesophageal carcinoma
qualifiers.shift: Solids alone suggests a mechanical narrowing; solids and liquids from the outset suggests a motility disorder such as achalasia. Progression from solids to liquids suggests a growing obstruction
qualifiers.misuse: Not distinguished from odynophagia, which is painful swallowing and has a different differential

qualifiers.name: Regurgitation of undigested food
qualifiers.definition: Return of unswallowed food without acid or bile
qualifiers.established: Ask whether the material tastes sour; undigested and non-acidic points above the stomach
qualifiers.example: dysphagia to solids and liquids with regurgitation of undigested food → achalasia
qualifiers.shift: Non-acidic undigested material localises the problem above the lower oesophageal sphincter, which separates it from the acid regurgitation of reflux
qualifiers.misuse: Called vomiting, which implies gastric contents and misdirects the differential

qualifiers.name: Amenorrhea
qualifiers.definition: Absence of menstruation
qualifiers.established: Establish primary versus secondary, and always send a pregnancy test first
qualifiers.associated: Pregnancy, hypothalamic amenorrhoea, polycystic ovary syndrome, hyperprolactinaemia, premature ovarian insufficiency, thyroid disease
qualifiers.example: amenorrhoea with galactorrhoea and a raised prolactin → prolactinoma
qualifiers.shift: Pregnancy first, always. After that the workup splits by FSH and prolactin, which separates ovarian failure from hypothalamic-pituitary causes
qualifiers.misuse: Investigated hormonally before a pregnancy test, which is both the commonest cause and the cheapest test

qualifiers.name: Galactorrhea
qualifiers.definition: Milky nipple discharge unrelated to breastfeeding
qualifiers.established: Confirm the discharge is milky and non-bloody; check both breasts and send prolactin
qualifiers.associated: Prolactinoma, antipsychotics and other dopamine antagonists, hypothyroidism, chest wall stimulation
qualifiers.example: galactorrhoea with amenorrhoea and visual field loss → prolactinoma
qualifiers.shift: With amenorrhoea it points at hyperprolactinaemia, and with a bitemporal field defect it localises to a pituitary macroadenoma. Bloody unilateral discharge is a different problem and suggests malignancy
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to a drug without measuring prolactin, so a macroadenoma compressing the chiasm goes undetected

qualifiers.name: Iron deficiency
qualifiers.definition: Depleted body iron stores, with or without anaemia
qualifiers.established: Ferritin with transferrin saturation and CRP, since ferritin rises with inflammation
qualifiers.associated: Blood loss, malabsorption, dietary deficiency, coeliac disease, gastrointestinal malignancy
qualifiers.example: iron deficiency in an adult man → gastrointestinal malignancy until excluded
qualifiers.shift: In an adult man or a postmenopausal woman, iron deficiency is gastrointestinal blood loss until endoscopy says otherwise. The deficiency itself is easy; the cause is the diagnosis
qualifiers.misuse: Corrected with iron without investigating the cause, which treats the number and misses the tumour

qualifiers.name: Low ferritin
qualifiers.definition: Serum ferritin below the reference range
qualifiers.established: Serum ferritin with CRP; a low value is specific for depleted stores even when the count is normal
qualifiers.example: hypochromic microcytic anaemia with low ferritin → iron deficiency
qualifiers.shift: A low ferritin is close to diagnostic of iron deficiency, but a normal or raised ferritin does not exclude it, because ferritin is an acute phase reactant. In inflammation, interpret it against a raised cut-off of around 100 alongside transferrin saturation and CRP; no single index is reliable alone, since inflammation depresses transferrin saturation too
qualifiers.misuse: A normal ferritin taken to exclude deficiency in an inflamed patient, which is where the test fails

qualifiers.name: Worsening oxygenation
qualifiers.definition: A sustained rise in the oxygen or PEEP requirement after a period of stability
qualifiers.established: Track FiO2 and PEEP over days rather than reading a single value
qualifiers.associated: Ventilator-associated pneumonia, ARDS progression, atelectasis, fluid overload, pulmonary embolism
qualifiers.example: sustained worsening of oxygenation after two stable days on the ventilator → ventilator-associated event
qualifiers.shift: Deliberately objective, because clinical pneumonia criteria in ventilated patients proved unreliable. The requirement for prior stability is what makes deterioration meaningful
qualifiers.misuse: Read from a single blood gas, which cannot distinguish a transient change from a sustained one

qualifiers.name: Subtherapeutic anticoagulation
qualifiers.definition: Anticoagulant effect below the intended range
qualifiers.established: INR for warfarin, adherence and dosing history for a direct oral anticoagulant, where no routine level exists
qualifiers.associated: Prosthetic valve thrombosis, recurrent venous thromboembolism, cardioembolic stroke
qualifiers.example: new heart failure with muffled prosthetic sounds and subtherapeutic anticoagulation → prosthetic valve thrombosis
qualifiers.shift: Converts an unexplained deterioration in a patient with a mechanical valve or prior thrombosis into a mechanical question with a time-critical answer
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed adequate on a direct oral anticoagulant because no level is checked; adherence is the variable to ask about. Note that direct oral anticoagulants are contraindicated in mechanical prosthetic valves, where warfarin is the only option

qualifiers.name: Elective
qualifiers.definition: A procedure that can safely be scheduled at a time of choosing
qualifiers.established: Judged on whether delay changes outcome, not on how the patient feels about waiting
qualifiers.associated: Hernia repair, joint replacement, planned cholecystectomy
qualifiers.example: elective repair of an asymptomatic hernia → observation is also reasonable
qualifiers.shift: Sets the whole risk calculation. Elective timing permits optimisation of anaemia, glycaemic control and anticoagulation, none of which is possible in an emergency, which is why elective mortality is a fraction of emergency mortality for the same operation
qualifiers.misuse: Applied to a condition that is quietly progressing; an incarcerating hernia is not elective merely because it has not strangulated yet

qualifiers.name: Urgent
qualifiers.definition: Requiring intervention within hours to days, sooner than a scheduled list allows
qualifiers.established: Judged on the rate at which the underlying process is progressing
qualifiers.associated: Obstructing stone with infection, acute cholecystitis, appendicitis, ascending cholangitis. Uncomplicated symptomatic gallstones are elective
qualifiers.example: urgent decompression of an infected obstructed kidney → emergency drainage
qualifiers.shift: The middle category, and the one most often mishandled, because it permits some optimisation but not a full workup. The question is what deteriorates while you wait
qualifiers.misuse: Collapsed into elective because the patient is currently stable, which ignores the trajectory

qualifiers.name: Emergent
qualifiers.definition: Requiring immediate intervention for an immediate threat to life, organ or limb
qualifiers.established: Judged at the bedside; the decision precedes complete information
qualifiers.associated: Ruptured aneurysm, necrotising fasciitis, acute limb ischaemia, testicular torsion, tension pneumothorax
qualifiers.example: emergent exploration for pain out of proportion with crepitus → necrotising fasciitis
qualifiers.shift: Inverts the usual order: intervention precedes complete diagnosis, because in these specific conditions the time cost of certainty exceeds the cost of a negative exploration. Waiting for imaging is itself a decision
qualifiers.misuse: Delayed for confirmatory imaging in conditions where the diagnosis is clinical and the imaging changes nothing

qualifiers.name: Curative intent
qualifiers.definition: Treatment aimed at eradicating disease and achieving long-term cure
qualifiers.established: Established by stage, performance status and the multidisciplinary plan; must be stated explicitly
qualifiers.associated: Early-stage solid tumours, some haematologic malignancies
qualifiers.example: curative intent chemoradiotherapy for localised disease → definitive treatment
qualifiers.shift: Determines how much toxicity is justified and how aggressively complications are managed. Intent should be documented, because it governs escalation decisions later when the patient may not be able to participate
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed by patients when it has not been stated; ambiguity here produces profound misunderstanding about prognosis

qualifiers.name: Palliative intent
qualifiers.definition: Treatment aimed at controlling disease and relieving symptoms where cure is not expected
qualifiers.established: Established by stage and multidisciplinary consensus; distinct from end-of-life or hospice care
qualifiers.associated: Metastatic solid tumours, advanced organ failure
qualifiers.example: palliative intent systemic therapy for metastatic disease → symptom control and survival extension
qualifiers.shift: Not the same as stopping treatment. Palliative intent chemotherapy can extend survival substantially, and conflating the two causes patients to refuse treatment that would help them
qualifiers.misuse: Equated with hospice or with giving up, which is the commonest and most damaging misunderstanding in oncology

qualifiers.name: Clean-contaminated
qualifiers.definition: An operation entering the respiratory, alimentary, genital or urinary tract under controlled conditions without unusual contamination
qualifiers.established: Assigned intraoperatively using the standard four-category wound classification
qualifiers.associated: Elective colorectal, biliary and pulmonary surgery
qualifiers.example: clean-contaminated colorectal resection → prophylactic antibiotics
qualifiers.shift: Sits second in the four-category scale used for surgical site infection surveillance and prophylaxis. The categories predict infection risk, which is why they are recorded rather than described
qualifiers.misuse: Assigned from the planned operation rather than what actually happened, which corrupts surveillance data

qualifiers.name: Contaminated
qualifiers.definition: An operation with a major break in sterile technique, gross spillage from a hollow viscus, or entry into acutely inflamed tissue without pus
qualifiers.established: Assigned intraoperatively
qualifiers.associated: Open fresh accidental wounds, gross gastrointestinal spillage, acute non-purulent inflammation. Perforated viscera are classed dirty-infected, not contaminated
qualifiers.example: contaminated field after gross enteric spillage → lavage with prophylaxis continued to 24 hours
qualifiers.shift: Third of the four categories, carrying substantially higher infection risk and changing wound management. Wound class alone does not make antibiotics therapeutic: only established infection does
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded as clean-contaminated to avoid the appearance of a complication, which distorts the record

qualifiers.name: Dirty-infected
qualifiers.definition: An operation on tissue with existing clinical infection, established pus, or perforated viscera with devitalised tissue
qualifiers.established: Assigned intraoperatively
qualifiers.associated: Perforated appendicitis with abscess, necrotising infection, delayed traumatic wounds
qualifiers.example: dirty field with established pus → source control and therapeutic antibiotics
qualifiers.shift: The highest-risk category, where antibiotics are therapeutic rather than prophylactic and primary closure is often avoided
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with contaminated; the presence of established pus or devitalised tissue is what separates them

qualifiers.name: Closed-loop obstruction
qualifiers.definition: A bowel segment obstructed at two points, so it can decompress in neither direction
qualifiers.established: CT showing a distended fluid-filled loop with two transition points, often with mesenteric changes
qualifiers.example: closed-loop obstruction on CT → emergency surgery
qualifiers.shift: Progresses rapidly to ischaemia and perforation because the trapped segment cannot vent. It is a surgical emergency, unlike simple obstruction which is often managed non-operatively
qualifiers.misuse: Managed conservatively as a simple obstruction, which is how a viable bowel loop is lost

qualifiers.name: Source-controlled
qualifiers.definition: The anatomical focus driving infection has been drained, removed or diverted
qualifiers.established: Confirmed by the procedure performed and by clinical and biochemical response
qualifiers.associated: Abscess, infected device, obstructed urinary or biliary tract, perforation
qualifiers.example: persistent fever on appropriate antibiotics → uncontrolled source
qualifiers.shift: One of the strongest modifiable determinants of outcome in surgical infection, and an independent predictor of survival when it is timely and adequate. Antibiotics cannot sterilise an undrained collection or an infected device, so failure to improve should prompt a search for an uncontrolled source rather than an antibiotic change
qualifiers.misuse: Escalating antibiotics for ongoing sepsis while the collection remains undrained

qualifiers.name: Well-appearing
qualifiers.definition: Comfortable and not distressed
qualifiers.established: End-of-bed assessment, weighed against vital signs
qualifiers.example: well appearance → self-limited illness
qualifiers.shift: Genuinely reassuring in most contexts, but a documented trap in early sepsis, compensated shock in the young, and mesenteric ischemia. Never allow it to override an abnormal physiologic parameter.
qualifiers.misuse: Used to override abnormal physiology; a documented trap in early sepsis and mesenteric ischemia

qualifiers.name: Cachectic
qualifiers.definition: Marked muscle and fat wasting
qualifiers.established: Inspection plus documented weight trajectory
qualifiers.associated: Malignancy, advanced heart or lung disease, HIV
qualifiers.example: cachexia → malignancy or advanced organ failure
qualifiers.shift: Implies a catabolic process over months and raises malignancy, chronic infection, and advanced organ failure. Independently predicts poor outcomes.

qualifiers.name: Diaphoretic
qualifiers.definition: Profusely sweating
qualifiers.established: Inspection and touch
qualifiers.associated: ACS, hypoglycemia, sepsis, thyroid storm, withdrawal
qualifiers.example: diaphoresis with chest pain → acute myocardial infarction
qualifiers.shift: A sympathetic surge. In chest pain it meaningfully raises the likelihood of infarction.

qualifiers.name: Icteric
qualifiers.definition: Yellow discoloration of sclerae and skin
qualifiers.established: Inspect the sclerae in natural light
qualifiers.example: scleral icterus → hyperbilirubinemia
qualifiers.shift: Detectable in the sclerae at lower bilirubin levels than in skin, so scleral examination is the more sensitive test.
qualifiers.misuse: Skin inspected instead; sclerae are more sensitive and less affected by skin tone

qualifiers.name: Central cyanosis
qualifiers.definition: Bluish discoloration of lips, tongue, and mucous membranes
qualifiers.established: Inspect the tongue and oral mucosa
qualifiers.example: central cyanosis → arterial hypoxemia or methemoglobinemia
qualifiers.shift: Reflects arterial desaturation and is a systemic problem. Requires roughly 5 g/dL of deoxygenated hemoglobin, so it appears late in anemia and early in polycythemia.
qualifiers.misuse: Requires about 5 g/dL of deoxygenated hemoglobin, so it appears late in anemia

qualifiers.name: Peripheral cyanosis
qualifiers.definition: Bluish discoloration of extremities only
qualifiers.established: Compare peripheries with the tongue
qualifiers.associated: Low output, cold exposure, peripheral vascular disease
qualifiers.example: peripheral cyanosis with warm core → low cardiac output
qualifiers.shift: Reflects increased peripheral extraction with normal arterial saturation. A perfusion problem, not an oxygenation problem.

qualifiers.name: Clubbing
qualifiers.definition: Loss of the nail-fold angle with increased nail bed fluctuance
qualifiers.established: Schamroth window and nail bed fluctuance
qualifiers.associated: Bronchiectasis, lung cancer, ILD, cyanotic heart disease, cirrhosis, IBD
qualifiers.example: clubbing in a smoker with dyspnea → lung cancer or bronchiectasis
qualifiers.shift: Notably absent in uncomplicated COPD and asthma, so its presence in a smoker with dyspnea should redirect toward malignancy, bronchiectasis, or fibrosis.
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to COPD, which does not cause clubbing

qualifiers.name: Pitting edema
qualifiers.definition: Indentation persists after pressure
qualifiers.established: Sustained pressure for at least ten seconds over a bony prominence
qualifiers.associated: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, venous disease
qualifiers.example: bilateral pitting edema → heart failure
qualifiers.shift: Indicates increased interstitial water with low protein content. Combined with laterality it is highly directive: bilateral pitting suggests systemic causes, unilateral suggests venous obstruction.
qualifiers.misuse: Pressed too briefly, so pitting is missed

qualifiers.name: Nonpitting edema
qualifiers.definition: No indentation after pressure
qualifiers.established: Sustained pressure producing no indentation
qualifiers.example: nonpitting limb swelling → lymphedema
qualifiers.shift: Redirects away from the common cardiac and renal causes toward lymphatic obstruction and thyroid disease, an entirely different workup.
qualifiers.misuse: Diuretics given for lymphedema, which does not respond

qualifiers.name: Anasarca
qualifiers.definition: Generalized massive edema including trunk and face
qualifiers.established: Examination of dependent areas, trunk, and face
qualifiers.associated: Nephrotic syndrome, severe heart failure, hepatic failure
qualifiers.example: anasarca → nephrotic syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Implies severe hypoalbuminemia or profound volume overload and marks advanced disease.

qualifiers.name: Fluctuant
qualifiers.definition: Palpable wave of contained fluid
qualifiers.established: Bimanual palpation for a transmitted fluid wave, or ultrasound
qualifiers.example: fluctuant swelling → abscess
qualifiers.shift: Indicates a drainable collection. Antibiotics alone are usually insufficient; this is a procedural finding.

qualifiers.name: Indurated
qualifiers.definition: Firm, thickened tissue without discrete fluid
qualifiers.established: Palpation for firmness without a fluid wave
qualifiers.example: induration without fluctuance → cellulitis
qualifiers.shift: Suggests inflammatory infiltration or fibrosis rather than a drainable collection.

qualifiers.name: Fixed
qualifiers.definition: Not mobile relative to surrounding tissue
qualifiers.established: Attempt to move the node against underlying tissue
qualifiers.example: fixed hard node → metastatic carcinoma
qualifiers.shift: Suggests invasion beyond the capsule. A hard, fixed, nontender node is a malignancy concern until proven otherwise.

qualifiers.name: Mobile
qualifiers.definition: Moves freely under the skin
qualifiers.established: Palpation assessing mobility and consistency
qualifiers.example: mobile rubbery node → reactive lymphadenopathy
qualifiers.shift: Suggests a lesion that has not invaded its surroundings, and generally favors a benign process.

qualifiers.name: Matted
qualifiers.definition: Multiple nodes adherent to one another
qualifiers.established: Palpation for adherence between adjacent nodes
qualifiers.example: matted cervical nodes → tuberculous lymphadenitis
qualifiers.shift: Implies periadenitis and capsular breach. Uncommon in reactive lymphadenopathy and should prompt biopsy.

qualifiers.name: Bruit
qualifiers.definition: Turbulent vascular sound on auscultation
qualifiers.established: Auscultate with the bell during held breath
qualifiers.associated: Carotid stenosis, renal artery stenosis, AV fistula
qualifiers.example: carotid bruit → carotid stenosis
qualifiers.shift: Indicates turbulent flow but correlates imperfectly with stenosis severity; a very tight stenosis may be silent.
qualifiers.misuse: Correlates poorly with severity; a critical stenosis may be silent

qualifiers.name: Thrill
qualifiers.definition: Palpable vibration over a vessel or the precordium
qualifiers.established: Palpate the precordium with the palm
qualifiers.associated: Severe valvular lesions, VSD, AV fistula
qualifiers.example: systolic thrill → severe valvular lesion or VSD
qualifiers.shift: A palpable thrill corresponds to at least a grade 4 murmur and reliably indicates a hemodynamically significant lesion.

qualifiers.name: Febrile
qualifiers.definition: Temperature above 38 degrees, or a documented fever in the recent history
qualifiers.established: Measured temperature, plus asking about fevers at home and antipyretic use
qualifiers.associated: Infection, malignancy, thromboembolism, drug reaction, autoimmune disease
qualifiers.example: febrile with a new murmur → infective endocarditis
qualifiers.shift: Raises infection but does not establish it. The other four causes of fever are commonly forgotten, and in an inpatient with negative cultures they become the differential
qualifiers.misuse: Equated with infection, which drives unnecessary antimicrobial escalation

qualifiers.name: Afebrile
qualifiers.definition: No fever documented across the illness
qualifiers.established: Serial temperature measurement rather than a single reading, with a medication review
qualifiers.example: afebrile with erythema and no antibiotic response → inflammatory breast carcinoma
qualifiers.shift: Argues against but does not exclude infection. Steroids, antipyretics, chronic kidney disease, and old age blunt the febrile response
qualifiers.misuse: Used to exclude sepsis in the elderly, who frequently mount no fever

qualifiers.name: Hemodynamically stable
qualifiers.definition: Perfusion adequate without vasoactive support
qualifiers.established: Blood pressure, heart rate, mentation, urine output, and lactate together
qualifiers.example: hemodynamically stable with no neurologic deficit → hold antibiotics for a micro diagnosis
qualifiers.shift: Permits a diagnostic pause. In vertebral osteomyelitis and endocarditis, stability is what buys time to culture before treating
qualifiers.misuse: Read from blood pressure alone, missing compensated shock in the young

qualifiers.name: Hemodynamically unstable
qualifiers.definition: Perfusion failing, with hypotension or evidence of end-organ hypoperfusion
qualifiers.established: Blood pressure with lactate, mentation, and urine output
qualifiers.associated: Sepsis, hemorrhage, tamponade, massive embolism, arrhythmia
qualifiers.example: hemodynamically unstable with elevated JVP → obstructive shock
qualifiers.shift: Removes the diagnostic pause and converts the workup into resuscitation. It also selects therapy: instability is what makes an embolism massive and a tachycardia a candidate for cardioversion
qualifiers.misuse: Waiting for hypotension, when narrowing pulse pressure and rising lactate come first

qualifiers.name: Multisystem
qualifiers.definition: Two or more organ systems involved by one process
qualifiers.established: Deliberate review across systems rather than following the presenting complaint
qualifiers.associated: Vasculitis, lupus, sarcoidosis, sepsis, lymphoma, endocarditis
qualifiers.example: rash with nephritis and neuropathy → systemic vasculitis
qualifiers.shift: The most useful trigger to abandon local explanations and look for a unifying diagnosis. One process explaining three systems beats three coincidences
qualifiers.misuse: Each system worked up by a different specialty, so the unifying pattern is never assembled

qualifiers.name: Euvolemic
qualifiers.definition: Normal effective circulating volume
qualifiers.established: JVP, skin turgor, mucous membranes, orthostatic vitals, weight trend
qualifiers.example: euvolemic hyponatremia → SIADH
qualifiers.shift: Volume status is the first branch point in hyponatremia and determines the entire subsequent workup and treatment
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed by one sign alone; clinical volume assessment is unreliable unless several findings are combined

qualifiers.name: Hypovolemic
qualifiers.definition: Reduced intravascular volume
qualifiers.established: Flat JVP, orthostatic change, dry membranes, low urine sodium
qualifiers.example: hypovolemic hyponatremia → gastrointestinal losses
qualifiers.shift: Directs toward saline rather than fluid restriction, the opposite of the treatment for SIADH
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with SIADH, and treating one as the other makes the sodium worse

qualifiers.name: Hypervolemic
qualifiers.definition: Excess total body fluid
qualifiers.established: Elevated JVP, edema, ascites, weight gain, crackles
qualifiers.example: hypervolemic hyponatremia → decompensated heart failure
qualifiers.shift: Indicates the effective arterial volume is low despite total body overload, which is why these patients are both wet and sodium-avid
qualifiers.misuse: Total body water and effective circulating volume conflated, which makes the physiology look contradictory

qualifiers.name: Serous
qualifiers.definition: Thin clear fluid
qualifiers.established: Direct inspection of drainage
qualifiers.example: serous wound drainage → seroma
qualifiers.shift: Argues against infection, which typically produces purulent or turbid fluid

qualifiers.name: Serosanguineous
qualifiers.definition: Mixed thin fluid and blood
qualifiers.established: Direct inspection of drainage
qualifiers.example: serosanguineous drainage → expected postoperative finding
qualifiers.shift: Usually expected early after surgery. A change from serosanguineous to purulent is the finding that matters

qualifiers.name: Kussmaul breathing
qualifiers.definition: Deep, laboured, regular hyperpnoea driven by metabolic acidosis
qualifiers.established: Observe depth rather than rate; the pattern is deep and sighing, not merely fast
qualifiers.associated: Diabetic ketoacidosis, uraemia, salicylate toxicity, lactic acidosis
qualifiers.example: Kussmaul breathing → diabetic ketoacidosis
qualifiers.shift: Signals a respiratory compensation for a metabolic acidosis, so the tachypnoea is appropriate rather than primary. Sedating or intubating such a patient removes the compensation and can precipitate collapse
qualifiers.misuse: Confused with Kussmaul sign, an unrelated rise in jugular venous pressure on inspiration

qualifiers.name: Murphy sign positive
qualifiers.definition: Arrest of inspiration on palpation beneath the right costal margin
qualifiers.established: Palpate at the right costal margin and ask the patient to breathe in
qualifiers.example: Murphy sign positive → acute cholecystitis
qualifiers.shift: Localizes right upper quadrant pain to an inflamed gallbladder rather than the liver or biliary tree, and a sonographic Murphy sign is more reliable than the bedside one
qualifiers.misuse: Poor sensitivity in the elderly and in those on analgesia; a negative sign does not exclude cholecystitis

qualifiers.name: Raynaud phenomenon
qualifiers.definition: Episodic digital colour change, classically white then blue then red, provoked by cold or stress
qualifiers.established: Ask for the triphasic colour change and its triggers; photographs from the patient are often more reliable than recollection
qualifiers.associated: Systemic sclerosis, lupus, mixed connective tissue disease, primary Raynaud, vibration injury
qualifiers.example: Raynaud with sclerodactyly → systemic sclerosis
qualifiers.shift: Primary and secondary Raynaud are separated by nailfold capillaroscopy and autoantibodies. Onset after 30, asymmetry, or digital ulceration all point at a secondary cause
qualifiers.misuse: Any cold hands called Raynaud; the finding requires demarcated colour change, not simply discomfort

qualifiers.name: Crepitus
qualifiers.definition: A crackling or grating sensation felt on palpation
qualifiers.established: Palpate the affected tissue or joint through a range of movement
qualifiers.associated: Subcutaneous emphysema, necrotizing fasciitis, osteoarthritis, fracture
qualifiers.example: crepitus with pain out of proportion → necrotizing fasciitis
qualifiers.shift: Meaning depends entirely on the tissue. In soft tissue with systemic toxicity it suggests gas-forming infection and is a surgical emergency; in a joint it is a benign degenerative finding
qualifiers.misuse: Soft tissue and joint crepitus treated as the same finding when they carry opposite urgency

qualifiers.name: Tracheal deviation
qualifiers.definition: Displacement of the trachea from the midline at the suprasternal notch
qualifiers.established: Palpate the trachea in the suprasternal notch with the neck neutral
qualifiers.associated: Tension pneumothorax, large pleural effusion, lobar collapse, mediastinal mass
qualifiers.example: tracheal deviation with hypotension → tension pneumothorax
qualifiers.shift: Direction discriminates: pushed away by a space-occupying process such as tension pneumothorax or effusion, pulled toward by volume loss such as collapse or fibrosis
qualifiers.misuse: Relied on in tension pneumothorax, where it is a late and insensitive sign; do not wait for it before decompressing

qualifiers.name: Cold and clammy
qualifiers.definition: Cool, pale, sweaty peripheries with delayed capillary refill
qualifiers.established: Touch the knees and feet, assess capillary refill centrally and peripherally
qualifiers.associated: Cardiogenic shock, hypovolaemic shock, obstructive shock
qualifiers.example: cold and clammy with hypotension → cardiogenic shock
qualifiers.shift: Splits shock at the bedside into low-output states, which vasoconstrict, and distributive states, which are warm and vasodilated. That distinction drives whether the answer is inotropy or vasopressors and fluids
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed in a cold room or in the elderly, where peripheral shutdown is not specific

qualifiers.name: Dry flushed skin
qualifiers.definition: Warm, dry, red skin with absent sweating
qualifiers.established: Feel the axilla, which stays dry in anticholinergic toxicity
qualifiers.example: dry flushed skin with delirium and mydriasis → anticholinergic toxicity
qualifiers.shift: The dryness is the discriminating half. Sympathomimetic toxicity produces an almost identical delirium and mydriasis but with drenching sweat, and the antidotes differ
qualifiers.misuse: Peripheral skin used instead of the axilla, where the difference is clearest

qualifiers.name: Otalgia
qualifiers.definition: Ear pain, either from the ear itself or referred along shared cranial nerve pathways
qualifiers.established: Examine the ear, then the throat, teeth, temporomandibular joint and neck when the ear looks normal
qualifiers.associated: Otitis media, otitis externa, malignant otitis externa, referred pain from pharyngeal or dental disease
qualifiers.example: severe otalgia with a normal ear drum → referred pain from a pharyngeal malignancy
qualifiers.shift: Pain with a normal-looking ear is referred until proven otherwise, which redirects the examination to the throat and teeth. Severe otalgia in a diabetic with granulation tissue at the bony junction is skull base osteomyelitis
qualifiers.misuse: Treated with topical drops without ever inspecting the pharynx, so a tumour presenting as ear pain is missed

qualifiers.name: Trismus
qualifiers.definition: Restricted mouth opening from spasm or mechanical limitation of the muscles of mastication
qualifiers.established: Ask the patient to open fully and measure the interincisal distance; under about 35 mm is restricted
qualifiers.associated: Peritonsillar abscess, Ludwig angina, deep neck space infection, tetanus, temporomandibular disorder
qualifiers.example: odynophagia with trismus → peritonsillar abscess
qualifiers.shift: In an infected throat this signals spread beyond the tonsil into the parapharyngeal space, which changes management from oral antibiotics to drainage and airway vigilance
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to pain alone; true trismus reflects muscle involvement and is a red flag for deep space infection

qualifiers.name: Uvular deviation
qualifiers.definition: Displacement of the uvula away from the midline
qualifiers.established: Inspect the oropharynx with a tongue depressor and good light
qualifiers.associated: Peritonsillar abscess, ninth and tenth cranial nerve palsy
qualifiers.example: uvular deviation with trismus and a muffled voice → peritonsillar abscess
qualifiers.shift: Static deviation away from the affected side indicates a unilateral space-occupying process, which distinguishes abscess from simple tonsillitis. On phonation the uvula is instead pulled away from the paralysed side, which is how a vagal palsy declares itself
qualifiers.misuse: Not looked for, because trismus makes the examination difficult exactly when the finding matters most

qualifiers.name: Drooling
qualifiers.definition: Inability or unwillingness to swallow saliva
qualifiers.established: Observe; a patient who will not swallow their own secretions is telling you something about the airway
qualifiers.associated: Epiglottitis, retropharyngeal abscess, Ludwig angina, oesophageal foreign body, severe odynophagia
qualifiers.example: drooling with tripoding and fever → epiglottitis
qualifiers.shift: In a febrile patient this signals impending airway compromise and stops routine throat examination, especially in children; in adults, visualisation should occur only where the airway can be secured. Involve anaesthesia and ENT
qualifiers.misuse: Provoked by attempting to examine the throat, which can precipitate obstruction in a child with epiglottitis

qualifiers.name: Tripoding
qualifiers.definition: Sitting forward on the hands with the neck extended and chin thrust forward to maximise airway calibre
qualifiers.established: Observe posture from the end of the bed before touching the patient
qualifiers.example: tripoding with drooling → epiglottitis
qualifiers.shift: A posture the patient adopts because it is the only one that works, which means the airway is marginal. Together with drooling it is an airway emergency
qualifiers.misuse: Interpreted as anxiety, and the patient laid flat, which can close a marginal airway

qualifiers.name: Muffled voice
qualifiers.definition: A thickened, hot-potato quality to the voice without hoarseness
qualifiers.established: Listen while the patient speaks; distinguish from the hoarseness of laryngeal disease
qualifiers.associated: Peritonsillar abscess, epiglottitis, deep neck space infection
qualifiers.example: muffled voice with trismus → peritonsillar abscess
qualifiers.shift: Localises the problem above the larynx, in the pharynx or supraglottis. Hoarseness localises to the vocal cords instead, which is a different differential entirely
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded as hoarseness; the two point at different anatomical levels

qualifiers.name: Conductive hearing loss
qualifiers.definition: Impaired transmission of sound through the external or middle ear
qualifiers.established: Weber lateralises to the affected ear and Rinne is negative on that side, with bone conduction better than air
qualifiers.associated: Cerumen impaction, otitis media with effusion, tympanic perforation, otosclerosis, cholesteatoma
qualifiers.example: conductive hearing loss with Weber lateralising to the affected ear → middle ear effusion
qualifiers.shift: Points at a mechanical problem, most of which are visible on otoscopy and many of which are reversible. It separates cleanly from sensorineural loss at the bedside with two tuning fork tests
qualifiers.misuse: Tuning fork tests skipped, so a treatable wax or effusion is investigated as though it were nerve deafness

qualifiers.name: Sensorineural hearing loss
qualifiers.definition: Impaired function of the cochlea or the auditory nerve
qualifiers.established: Weber lateralises to the better ear and Rinne is positive bilaterally, with air conduction better than bone
qualifiers.associated: Presbycusis, noise exposure, sudden sensorineural hearing loss, acoustic neuroma, Meniere disease, ototoxicity
qualifiers.example: sudden unilateral sensorineural loss with Weber to the good ear → sudden sensorineural hearing loss
qualifiers.shift: Sudden unilateral loss is an emergency, because steroid treatment is time-dependent and works best within about two weeks of onset. Asymmetric loss also raises the question of a retrocochlear lesion
qualifiers.misuse: Assumed to be wax and given drops, wasting the treatment window in sudden sensorineural loss

qualifiers.name: Vertigo
qualifiers.definition: An illusion of movement, of self or surroundings
qualifiers.established: Ask what the patient means by dizzy; establish duration, triggers, and whether it is provoked by position change
qualifiers.associated: BPPV, vestibular neuritis, Meniere disease, cerebellar stroke, vestibular migraine
qualifiers.example: episodic positional vertigo lasting under a minute → benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
qualifiers.shift: Duration is the primary discriminator: seconds suggests BPPV, hours suggests Meniere, days suggests neuritis or stroke. Central causes are separated by the head impulse, nystagmus and skew examination, not by severity
qualifiers.misuse: Grouped with presyncope and unsteadiness under the word dizzy, which merges three different differentials

qualifiers.name: Tinnitus
qualifiers.definition: Perception of sound without an external source
qualifiers.established: Ask whether it is pulsatile and whether it is unilateral
qualifiers.associated: Presbycusis, noise exposure, Meniere disease, acoustic neuroma, ototoxicity; pulsatile suggests a vascular cause
qualifiers.example: unilateral pulsatile tinnitus → a venous sinus or dural arteriovenous cause
qualifiers.shift: Unilateral or pulsatile tinnitus needs imaging, because it suggests a structural or vascular lesion. Bilateral non-pulsatile tinnitus with symmetric hearing loss is usually presbycusis or noise damage
qualifiers.misuse: Dismissed as universal and benign, so the unilateral case that needed an MRI is not identified

qualifiers.name: Aural fullness
qualifiers.definition: A sensation of pressure or blockage in the ear
qualifiers.established: Ask about associated hearing change, vertigo and tinnitus; examine the drum and test hearing
qualifiers.associated: Meniere disease, otitis media with effusion, eustachian tube dysfunction, acoustic neuroma
qualifiers.example: aural fullness with episodic vertigo and fluctuating hearing loss → Meniere disease
qualifiers.shift: On its own it is nonspecific, but with fluctuating hearing loss, tinnitus and episodic vertigo it completes the Meniere tetrad
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to eustachian dysfunction without testing hearing, which is where the fluctuation would be documented

qualifiers.name: Absent cremasteric reflex
qualifiers.definition: Loss of the normal ipsilateral testicular elevation when the inner thigh is stroked
qualifiers.established: Stroke the medial thigh and watch for the testis to rise; compare with the unaffected side
qualifiers.example: absent cremasteric reflex with a high-riding testis → testicular torsion
qualifiers.shift: One of the most useful bedside signs in acute scrotal pain: sensitive but not specific, since it is also absent in epididymo-orchitis. Its absence in a painful hemiscrotum, with a supportive history and testicular lie, justifies exploration without waiting for imaging, because the salvage window is roughly six hours
qualifiers.misuse: Its presence taken to exclude torsion; the reflex can persist in torsion and is unreliable in boys under about 30 months

qualifiers.name: High-riding testis
qualifiers.definition: A testis sitting higher in the scrotum than its fellow, often with a transverse rather than vertical lie
qualifiers.established: Inspect and palpate both sides with the patient supine, comparing position and axis
qualifiers.example: high-riding transverse testis → testicular torsion
qualifiers.shift: Shortening of the cord by twisting raises and rotates the testis. With acute severe pain and an absent cremasteric reflex this is a surgical emergency, and imaging must not delay exploration
qualifiers.misuse: Sought only on the painful side; the finding is comparative and needs both sides examined

qualifiers.name: Perifollicular hemorrhage
qualifiers.definition: Pinpoint bleeding around hair follicles, often with surrounding corkscrew hairs
qualifiers.established: Inspect the shins and thighs in good light with the leg hair visible
qualifiers.example: perifollicular hemorrhage with corkscrew hairs → vitamin C deficiency
qualifiers.shift: Collagen synthesis fails without ascorbate, so capillaries around the follicle leak. With gingival bleeding and poor wound healing this is close to specific for scurvy, which is easy to miss because nobody expects it
qualifiers.misuse: Mistaken for vasculitis; the follicular centring and the coiled hair are what separate them

qualifiers.name: Corkscrew hairs
qualifiers.definition: Coiled, fragile body hairs, typically on the lower limbs
qualifiers.established: Inspect leg hair closely, ideally with a dermatoscope
qualifiers.example: corkscrew hairs → vitamin C deficiency
qualifiers.shift: A specific sign of defective collagen in the hair follicle. Alongside perifollicular haemorrhage it identifies scurvy in patients whose diet is not obviously deficient, particularly those with alcohol misuse, restrictive diets or isolation
qualifiers.misuse: Not looked for, because leg hair is rarely examined at all

qualifiers.name: Gingival bleeding
qualifiers.definition: Bleeding from the gums, spontaneously or on minimal contact
qualifiers.established: Inspect the gums; ask about bleeding on brushing
qualifiers.associated: Vitamin C deficiency, thrombocytopenia, leukaemia, von Willebrand disease, periodontal disease
qualifiers.example: gingival bleeding with corkscrew hairs → vitamin C deficiency
qualifiers.shift: Splits into a local periodontal cause and a systemic one. With mucocutaneous bleeding elsewhere it points at platelets or von Willebrand factor; with perifollicular haemorrhage it points at scurvy
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to poor dental hygiene without a blood count, which is where leukaemia occasionally presents

qualifiers.name: Diaphoresis
qualifiers.definition: Profuse sweating disproportionate to ambient temperature or exertion
qualifiers.established: Feel the skin, particularly the forehead and torso; note whether it is cold or warm
qualifiers.associated: Acute coronary syndrome, hypoglycaemia, sepsis, thyroid storm, phaeochromocytoma, serotonin syndrome, withdrawal
qualifiers.example: chest pain with diaphoresis → acute coronary syndrome
qualifiers.shift: With chest pain it modestly raises the probability of infarction, with a positive likelihood ratio around 2, and is among the more useful associated symptoms. Cold and clammy suggests sympathetic drive from a low-output state; warm and sweaty suggests fever or a toxidrome
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to anxiety, which is the interpretation that most often precedes a missed infarction

qualifiers.name: Pallor
qualifiers.definition: Abnormal paleness of skin and mucous membranes
qualifiers.established: Inspect conjunctivae, palmar creases and nail beds rather than facial skin
qualifiers.example: pallor with a rapid drop in haemoglobin → acute haemorrhage
qualifiers.shift: Insensitive for mild anaemia but meaningful when marked, particularly with tachycardia and hypotension, where it suggests acute blood loss rather than chronic anaemia
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed on facial skin, which reflects pigmentation and vasoconstriction more than haemoglobin

qualifiers.name: Petechiae
qualifiers.definition: Pinpoint non-blanching haemorrhages under 2 mm
qualifiers.established: Press with a glass slide to confirm non-blanching; inspect dependent areas, conjunctivae and palate
qualifiers.associated: Thrombocytopenia, meningococcaemia, vasculitis, endocarditis, mechanical from coughing or vomiting
qualifiers.example: non-blanching petechiae with fever → meningococcaemia
qualifiers.shift: Non-blanching is the whole finding. With fever it is a medical emergency until meningococcal disease is excluded, and it must not wait for a rash to become obvious
qualifiers.misuse: Assessed without a glass slide, so a blanching viral exanthem is confused with purpura or the reverse

qualifiers.name: Hyperpigmented
qualifiers.definition: Abnormally increased skin pigmentation, generalised or localised
qualifiers.established: Inspect palmar creases, buccal mucosa, scars and areolae, where adrenal pigmentation is most obvious
qualifiers.associated: Primary adrenal insufficiency, haemochromatosis, chronic kidney disease, drugs, Whipple disease
qualifiers.example: hyperpigmentation with hypotension and hyponatraemia → primary adrenal insufficiency
qualifiers.shift: Pigmentation in the creases and buccal mucosa reflects raised ACTH, which localises the lesion to the adrenal rather than the pituitary. Secondary adrenal insufficiency is not pigmented
qualifiers.misuse: Only sun-exposed skin examined, where pigmentation is uninterpretable

qualifiers.name: Pruritus
qualifiers.definition: Itch, with or without a visible rash
qualifiers.established: Establish whether there is a primary rash, whether it is worse after bathing, and whether it wakes the patient
qualifiers.associated: Cholestasis, uraemia, polycythaemia vera, Hodgkin lymphoma, atopic dermatitis, scabies, drugs
qualifiers.example: aquagenic pruritus with a raised haematocrit → polycythaemia vera
qualifiers.shift: Itch without a primary rash points at a systemic cause. Aquagenic itch after a warm bath is characteristic of polycythaemia vera, and nocturnal itch with burrows suggests scabies
qualifiers.misuse: Treated with emollients without ever asking whether there is a primary lesion, which is the branch point

qualifiers.name: Hyperthermia
qualifiers.definition: Core temperature elevation not mediated by the hypothalamic set point
qualifiers.established: Core temperature, ideally rectal or oesophageal, alongside the neuromuscular examination
qualifiers.associated: Heat stroke, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, serotonin syndrome, malignant hyperthermia, thyroid storm, anticholinergic toxicity
qualifiers.example: hyperthermia above 40 degrees with rigidity → neuroleptic malignant syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Distinct from fever, which is a regulated response. Hyperthermia does not respond to antipyretics and needs active cooling, and above 40 degrees with rigidity it is a toxicological emergency
qualifiers.misuse: Treated with paracetamol, which does nothing when the set point is not the problem

qualifiers.name: Hypotension
qualifiers.definition: Blood pressure below the level needed to perfuse organs for that patient
qualifiers.established: Measure with the correct cuff, check both arms, and compare with the patient's usual pressure
qualifiers.associated: Shock of any cause, adrenal crisis, sepsis, haemorrhage, drugs, tamponade
qualifiers.example: hypotension unresponsive to fluids with hyperpigmentation → adrenal crisis
qualifiers.shift: Absolute numbers matter less than the change from the patient's baseline and the evidence of hypoperfusion. Fluid responsiveness is itself diagnostic and separates hypovolaemic from cardiogenic and obstructive causes
qualifiers.misuse: Read as adequate because it exceeds an arbitrary threshold, in a chronically hypertensive patient for whom it is profound

qualifiers.name: Tachycardia
qualifiers.definition: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute
qualifiers.established: Pulse and ECG together; note whether it is regular and whether the complex is narrow or wide
qualifiers.associated: Sepsis, hypovolaemia, pain, anaemia, pulmonary embolism, thyrotoxicosis, arrhythmia, withdrawal
qualifiers.example: tachycardia with hypoxaemia and clear lungs → pulmonary embolism
qualifiers.shift: Almost always secondary, so the work is naming the cause. Regularity and complex width classify it, and a rate that does not respond to treating the presumed cause suggests the rhythm itself is primary
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as the problem rather than the response, so rate control masks the compensation for hypovolaemia

qualifiers.name: Absent pulses
qualifiers.definition: Loss of a palpable pulse in a limb
qualifiers.established: Palpate all limb pulses and compare sides; use a Doppler probe when palpation fails
qualifiers.associated: Acute limb ischaemia, aortic dissection, Takayasu arteritis, peripheral arterial disease, compartment syndrome
qualifiers.example: absent pulses with pain out of proportion → acute limb ischaemia
qualifiers.shift: With pain, pallor, paraesthesia, paralysis and perishing cold this completes acute limb ischaemia, where the window before irreversible muscle loss is roughly six hours. Asymmetric pulses also raise dissection
qualifiers.misuse: Documented without comparing sides or without a Doppler, so a critically ischaemic limb is recorded as pulses present

qualifiers.name: Pain out of proportion
qualifiers.definition: Pain markedly exceeding what the visible findings would explain
qualifiers.established: Compare the reported severity and analgesic requirement against the examination
qualifiers.associated: Necrotising fasciitis, acute mesenteric ischaemia, acute limb ischaemia, compartment syndrome
qualifiers.example: pain out of proportion with a raised lactate → acute mesenteric ischaemia
qualifiers.shift: One of the highest-yield red flags in medicine. Each of its causes is a surgical emergency in which the surface appearance lags far behind the tissue damage, so believing the examination over the pain is the error
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to drug seeking or low pain threshold, which is precisely how necrotising fasciitis is missed

qualifiers.name: Podagra
qualifiers.definition: Acute arthritis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint
qualifiers.established: Inspect and palpate the first MTP joint; aspirate where the diagnosis is uncertain
qualifiers.example: acute monoarticular podagra → gout
qualifiers.shift: Highly suggestive of gout, but the joint can be septic and the two coexist. Aspiration remains the arbiter, since crystals and infection are not mutually exclusive
qualifiers.misuse: Treated as gout without aspiration in a febrile patient, where a septic joint is missed

qualifiers.name: Pathergy
qualifiers.definition: Formation of a papule or pustule at the site of minor skin trauma such as a needle prick
qualifiers.established: Read the site of a sterile needle prick at 24 to 48 hours
qualifiers.associated: Behcet disease, pyoderma gangrenosum, Sweet syndrome
qualifiers.example: oral and genital ulceration with pathergy → Behcet disease
qualifiers.shift: Reflects a neutrophilic hyperreactivity, and in the right clinical setting it supports Behcet disease. It also warns against surgical debridement in pyoderma gangrenosum, where trauma enlarges the lesion
qualifiers.misuse: Debrided; in pyoderma gangrenosum surgery makes the ulcer worse, which is the practical reason the sign matters

qualifiers.name: Absent bowel sounds
qualifiers.definition: Silence on prolonged auscultation of the abdomen
qualifiers.established: Listen for at least two minutes in several quadrants before declaring absence
qualifiers.associated: Peritonitis, ileus, late bowel obstruction, mesenteric ischaemia
qualifiers.example: distended abdomen with absent bowel sounds and peritonism → perforation
qualifiers.shift: Silence with peritonism suggests an established peritoneal process, whereas high-pitched tinkling sounds suggest obstruction with a still-fighting bowel. The transition from tinkling to silence is a deterioration
qualifiers.misuse: Declared after fifteen seconds of listening, which is far too short to call absence

qualifiers.name: Distended
qualifiers.definition: Abdominal distension, from gas, fluid, mass or obstruction
qualifiers.established: Inspect, percuss for resonance versus shifting dullness, and palpate for masses
qualifiers.associated: Bowel obstruction, ascites, ileus, abdominal compartment syndrome, pregnancy, organomegaly
qualifiers.example: distended tense abdomen with oliguria and rising airway pressures → abdominal compartment syndrome
qualifiers.shift: Percussion note separates gas from fluid in seconds. Tense distension with organ dysfunction is abdominal compartment syndrome, which needs bladder pressure measurement rather than further imaging
qualifiers.misuse: Attributed to obesity without percussion, so ascites and obstruction are both missed

qualifiers.name: Volume overload
qualifiers.definition: Excess extracellular fluid, evident as oedema, raised venous pressure and pulmonary congestion
qualifiers.established: Jugular venous pressure, lung bases, peripheral and sacral oedema, weight trend
qualifiers.associated: Heart failure, renal failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, iatrogenic fluid
qualifiers.example: volume overload with a raised JVP → decompensated heart failure
qualifiers.shift: Distribution points at mechanism. A raised jugular venous pressure suggests a cardiac or renal cause, while oedema with a flat JVP and hypoalbuminaemia suggests a low oncotic pressure state such as nephrotic syndrome or cirrhosis
qualifiers.misuse: Diagnosed on ankle oedema alone, which is common, gravitational and frequently venous rather than cardiac

qualifiers.name: Crepitus, subcutaneous
qualifiers.definition: A crackling sensation on palpation of soft tissue, from gas within it
qualifiers.established: Palpate gently over the affected area and listen; imaging confirms and defines extent
qualifiers.associated: Necrotising fasciitis, Fournier gangrene, gas gangrene, pneumomediastinum, emphysematous infection
qualifiers.example: perineal pain out of proportion with crepitus → Fournier gangrene
qualifiers.shift: Gas in soft tissue implies a gas-forming organism or a communication with air, and with systemic toxicity it mandates immediate surgical exploration rather than imaging first
qualifiers.misuse: Absence relied on to exclude necrotising infection, where crepitus is present in a minority and appears late

qualifiers.name: Pain on tragal pressure
qualifiers.definition: Pain provoked by pressing the tragus or moving the pinna
qualifiers.established: Press the tragus and pull the pinna while watching the patient's face
qualifiers.example: otalgia with pain on tragal pressure and a normal drum → otitis externa
qualifiers.shift: Localises inflammation to the external canal rather than the middle ear, which separates otitis externa from otitis media in a single manoeuvre
qualifiers.misuse: Not performed, so canal and middle ear disease are treated identically

qualifiers.name: Blood pressure discrepancy
qualifiers.definition: A sustained difference in systolic pressure between the two arms
qualifiers.established: Measure both arms with the same correctly sized cuff, ideally simultaneously; over 15 mmHg is significant
qualifiers.associated: Aortic dissection, subclavian stenosis, Takayasu arteritis, large vessel giant cell arteritis, thoracic outlet syndrome
qualifiers.example: chest pain with a blood pressure discrepancy → aortic dissection
qualifiers.shift: Implies an obstructive lesion between the aortic root and one subclavian artery. In chest pain it raises dissection, and in a young patient without chest pain it raises large vessel arteritis
qualifiers.misuse: Measured sequentially in an anxious patient, where normal variation can exceed the threshold

qualifiers.name: Thompson test positive
qualifiers.definition: Absence of ankle plantarflexion when the calf is squeezed with the patient prone
qualifiers.established: Prone with feet over the end of the couch; squeeze the calf and watch the foot
qualifiers.example: a sudden calf pop with a positive Thompson test → Achilles tendon rupture
qualifiers.shift: Near-diagnostic at the bedside. Patients often still walk using the long flexors, which is exactly why the rupture is missed without this test
qualifiers.misuse: Not performed because the patient is ambulant, which is the commonest reason the diagnosis is delayed

qualifiers.name: Hypopyon
qualifiers.definition: A layer of white cells in the anterior chamber, visible as a fluid level
qualifiers.established: Inspect the anterior chamber with a light source; a slit lamp defines it
qualifiers.associated: Endophthalmitis, severe anterior uveitis, Behcet disease, corneal ulcer
qualifiers.example: painful visual loss with hypopyon after intraocular injection → endophthalmitis
qualifiers.shift: After an intraocular procedure this is endophthalmitis until proven otherwise and needs a vitreous tap and intravitreal antibiotics within hours, not a clinic appointment
qualifiers.misuse: Recorded without asking about recent intraocular surgery or injection, which is what makes it an emergency

qualifiers.name: Curtain-like field defect
qualifiers.definition: A progressive shadow advancing across the visual field
qualifiers.established: Ask the patient to describe the shape and direction of travel of the visual loss
qualifiers.example: floaters and photopsias then a curtain-like field defect → retinal detachment
qualifiers.shift: Distinguishes a detaching retina from the floaters of a posterior vitreous detachment alone. Macular involvement changes the urgency, because central vision once lost recovers poorly
qualifiers.misuse: Described as blurring, which loses the shape of the defect and therefore its localisation

qualifiers.name: Nonpitting
qualifiers.definition: Swelling that does not indent with sustained pressure
